items.title: Dolly Parton’s nephew ordered to stay away from her estate over alleged threats
items.description: Dolly Parton’s nephew has been ordered to stay away from employees and properties of her estate, US media reported, after the manager for the late country music legend alleged an “escalating campaign of threats” to extort money from the vast enterprise. Chancellor I’Ashea L. Myles of Nashville Chancery Court issued the temporary restraining order Wednesday, citing emails and other communications between the pair which involved “threats with demands for payment,” Rolling Stone magazine reported. Parton’s longtime manager Danny Nozell requested the restraining order, accusing the artist’s nephew, Bryan Seaver, of attempting to extort money from the estate, which includes an amusement park, a hotel and a soon-to-be-opened museum. Myles ordered Seaver to stay at least 1,000 feet (300 meters) from estate employees and business partners, remain off private property owned by the estate, and refrain from disruptive or harassing conduct, Rolling Stone reported, citing the ruling. Seaver’s statements were significant “not merely because of their language in isolation, but also because they were made in conjunction with statements threatening specific individuals and business interests associated with Ms. Parton’s professional property and estate,” Myles wrote. Myles has scheduled a hearing for October 7, according to the Davidson County Chancery Court website. Seaver, who broke the news of the singer’s death last month in an emotional video, had provided security for Parton for years but was abruptly fired last week, TMZ reported. That caused Seaver to criticize Nozell, with the outlet quoting Seaver as saying he was “dismayed by the unexpected and, so far, unexplained actions.” Court papers filed Tuesday allege that Seaver sent threats including a text message warning he would become “the hand of retribution for my entire family,” The New York Times reported. The paper said the request for a restraining order was filed in Nashville — Parton’s longtime home — by She’s Alive, the organization run by Nozell that manages her business empire. In a message sent to The New York Times, Seaver, who describes himself as a military contractor and international arms dealer, said he was carrying out his own probe into how his aunt’s affairs were being managed at the time of her death. Parton died last month aged 80, sparking mourning around the world for the singer who rose from grinding poverty to become a rhinestone-studded icon with hits like “Jolene” and “I Will Always Love You.” She also starred in Hollywood films and donated millions to charities. Her business empire is worth hundreds of millions of dollars and includes her popular Dollywood theme park, cosmetics, pet apparel, baking mixes and even a truck stop. The Dollywood theme park in Tennessee attracts around four million visitors a year and employs 4,000 people. items.title: Que révèle la « découverte » par Anthropic d’une nouvelle enzyme ?
items.description: L'annonce par Dario Amodei de la découverte, par Claude, d'une famille d'enzymes apparentée au système CRISPR relève au moins autant de la communication que de la science. Son message principal est simple : Anthropic dispose désormais de ses propres laboratoires de biologie, et entend capter une partie de la valeur que devraient générer les progrès médicaux permis par l'IA Claude discovers a novel enzyme system with CRISPR-like repeats , Anthropic, 23 septembre 2026.'> 1 . Le message publié par le PDG d'Anthropic sur X compte 715 mots, sur lesquels seulement 101 portent sur la découverte elle-même, et 614 visent à répondre par avance à ceux qui seraient tentés d'en minimiser la portée. Today we announced the Claude-led discovery of a molecular machine that we suspect could represent a new gene editing mechanism. Its precise function, biotechnological utility (if any), or level of significance is not yet clear, but at minimum it is work I would have been proud… https://t.co/hyzhzirNJe — Dario Amodei (@DarioAmodei) September 23, 2026 Son argumentaire s'appuie sur la progression de l'IA en mathématiques, passée en quelques années de contributions marginales à des avancées majeures, ainsi que sur son essai de 2024, Machines of Loving Grace , dans lequel il affirmait que l'IA pourrait condenser en 5 à 10 ans des décennies de progrès en biologie et en médecine. Il fait valoir que, quand bien même cette découverte serait mineure, elle ne constituerait qu'un point de départ, sur une trajectoire comparable à celle observée en mathématiques. La prépublication de l'article scientifique qui présente ces travaux reflète le même déséquilibre. Les chercheurs d’Anthropic ont ainsi demandé à Claude d'identifier de nouveaux gènes appartenant à la famille des transcriptases inverses et. al. , « Autonomous AI agents discover reverse transcriptases with tandem repeat arrays », Anthropic, 23 septembre 2026.'> 2 . L'introduction ne justifie toutefois jamais ce choix, alors que c'est elle qui, dans un article biomédical, pose d’ordinaire le contexte et fixe les objectifs. Les justifications possibles ne manquaient pourtant pas : la transcriptase inverse a un taux d'erreur élevé, ce qui explique en partie la forte fréquence de mutation de virus comme le VIH. De nouvelles variantes pourraient donc servir d'outils de mutagénèse dirigée. Surtout, Amodei lui-même rapproche ces enzymes de CRISPR, l'outil d'édition du génome qui a valu à Emmanuelle Charpentier et Jennifer Doudna le prix Nobel de chimie en 2020. Les auteurs auraient donc pu présenter leur recherche comme une piste vers de nouveaux outils d'édition, potentiellement plus précis que CRISPR, qui reste imparfait. La partie « discussion », d’ordinaire centrale dans un article biomédical, n’aborde pas davantage ces perspectives. L'article s'en tient au minimum sur le plan biologique, mais détaille longuement la manière dont Claude a procédé. Il existe des démonstrations solides du potentiel de l'IA en biomédecine. Pourtant, Amodei n'en mentionne aucune, et aucune ne vient d'Anthropic. La principale est AlphaFold, le modèle de Google DeepMind qui prédit la structure tridimensionnelle des protéines à partir de leur séquence. Si l’article cite AlphaFold, celui-ci ne constitue qu’un outil, et n'est jamais présenté pour ce qu'il est, soit la preuve la plus forte à ce jour de l'apport de l'IA à la biologie. Cet été, Moderna et Merck ont quant à eux publié des résultats intermédiaires prometteurs de l'essai de phase III de leur vaccin à ARN messager contre le cancer . La technologie de l'ARNm est antérieure à l'IA, mais le déploiement de ce traitement à grande échelle suppose d'y recourir pour accélérer la production et réduire les coûts. Là encore, Amodei n’en parle pas. Celui-ci n'affirme toutefois rien de faux, et le résultat n'est pas dénué d'intérêt : l'enzyme identifiée présente des similitudes avec CRISPR, mais aussi des différences qui pourraient la rendre utile. Claude semble avoir tiré des données génomiques une série de prédictions que les chercheurs n'ont eu qu'à vérifier expérimentalement, ce qui leur a évité de tester un grand nombre d'hypothèses. Mieux rédigé, et avec une réflexion et des perspectives plus développées, l'article aurait été tout à fait publiable. CRISPR, comme l’enzyme découverte ici, fait partie du « système immunitaire » que les bactéries utilisent pour se défendre contre les bactériophages, les virus qui les infectent. Ainsi, cette « découverte » pourrait potentiellement fournir de nouvelles cibles thérapeutiques. En effet, les bactéries du genre Staphylococcus semblent utiliser ces enzymes pour se défendre contre certaines infections de bactériophages. La découverte de ces enzymes, ainsi que l’étude de leur structure, pourraient donc permettre de concevoir des médicaments bloquant leur fonctionnement, rendant ainsi des bactéries telles que Staphylococcus aureus vulnérables aux infections de bactériophages. Cette « découverte » pourrait donc, en théorie, déboucher sur la mise au point de nouveaux antibiotiques, dont l’humanité a plus que jamais besoin étant donné le péril croissant de la résistance bactérienne. Amodei et les équipes d’Anthropic semblent toutefois avoir manqué cette opportunité. L’article Que révèle la « découverte » par Anthropic d’une nouvelle enzyme ? est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: Aubameyang to miss two months for Deportivo after knee surgery
items.description: Deportivo La Coruna striker Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang underwent knee surgery on Thursday, his club announced, and is expected to be out for two months. The 37-year-old had an operation on the meniscus in his right knee at a clinic in Madrid after feeling discomfort during Sunday’s draw with Real Betis. The club said Gabon’s all-time top scorer would return to La Coruna. “His progress will determine when he returns to training,” Deportivo said in a statement. The Spanish press reported that the former Arsenal and Chelsea player was expected to be sidelined for nearly two months. Aubameyang has scored five of his side’s 10 league goals as promoted Deportivo have made a strong start to the season. They sit seventh in La Liga with 10 points from seven games. He quit international duty earlier this month, saying he felt “humiliated” after the Gabonese government singled him out as responsible for a disappointing 2025 Africa Cup of Nations campaign. “We are grateful for what you have achieved” – AGI President tells Finance Minister
items.description: The President of the Association of Ghana Industries (AGI), Dr Kofi Nsiah-Poku, has commended Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson for the progress made in stabilising Ghana’s economy. He made the remarks during a meeting between the Finance Minister, the leadership of the AGI and leading captains of industry. “We are grateful for what you have achieved so far. We now know that we have achieved stability, and it is time for us to grow so that we can create jobs,” Dr Nsiah-Poku said. He noted that the progress made provides a strong foundation for the country’s next phase of economic development, with attention now turning to industrial expansion, exports and job creation. Dr Forson explained that the meeting formed part of the Government’s stakeholder engagements towards the preparation of the 2027 Budget. “We are preparing a new direction for the country. I called this meeting to engage you on what will help you expand, export more and create more jobs,” the Finance Minister said. The meeting underscored the Government’s commitment to working closely with industry to consolidate economic stability and translate it into stronger growth, increased exports and sustainable jobs for Ghanaians.

Shettima tasks Nigerians in US with backing Tinubu’s economic reforms
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA— THE Vice President, Senator Kashim Shettima has called on Nigerians in the diaspora, especially those in the United States, to support President Bola Tinubu’s administration in its efforts to transform the country’s economic fortunes. He said the administration was doing its best to reposition the economy particularly in the areas of education, health, science and technology, agriculture and would leverage the intellect of the diaspora community which according to him, is “the greatest resource of the future”. “Citizens of our country have the capacity and intellect to harness our nation’s potentials and take it to greater heights,” the VP added. Senator Shettima stated this on at the Nigeria House in New York during an interactive session with the Nigerian diaspora community in the United States. Speaking on some of the reforms undertaken by the current administration, the Vice President said President Tinubu has been courageous from the onset, which culminated in bold decisions has continued to reposition the economy. His words: “When President Tinubu assumed office, he did not resort to trading blames and accusing his predecessor for the state of affairs of our nation. Rather, he took decisions that only a leader of courage and conviction would take.” He, however, stated that the gains of the reforms undertaken were already yielding tangible results as evident in the increase in the country’s foreign reserves from 3.9 billion dollars to over 55 billion dollars and the 4.45 percent growth in the last quarter. He added that the improvements recorded in the exchange rate and foreign reserves on account of the refroms, would guarantee the safety of diaspora remittances, stability of the exchange rate and investments made by Nigerians in the diaspora. The Vice President stated that the administration of President Tinubu was determined to redefine the meaning of modern governance because the trajectory of global growth was facing Africa and that Nigeria has a big role to play in the emerging era. According to the VP, “We are working day and night to reposition the Nigerian nation as investment confidence is returning to Nigeria, and the Dangote Refinery success story is a true manifestation in recent times. “Be rest assured that beyond the negative stories that you hear and see in the social media, Nigeria is open for business. We have crossed the rubicon, and we are on the path of sustained growth.” Senator Shettima also spoke about the introduction of the Nigeria Education Loan Fund, where over 1.29 million Nigerian students in tertiary institutions have had access to N125 billion since the inception of the programme. On security challenges, the Vice President said though it is not peculiar to Nigeria alone, the administration was deploying all the means at its disposal to contain emerging challenges. He also urged concerned citizens to strive for a united and prosperous nation, noting that Nigerians must unite for the progress of their country, stating that “whatever binds us together supercedes whatever divides us as a people”. Also present at the event were Governors Babagana Zulum of Borno State; Abdulrahman AbdulRazaq of Kwara; Siminalayi Fubara of Rivers; Dauda Lawal of Zamfara; Senate Leader, Sen. Opeyemi Bamidele, and spouses of the Governors of Kwara, Katsina, Abia and Osun states. Others included, Ministers of Foreign Affairs, Amb. Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu; Science, Innovation and Technology, Dr. Kingsley Tochukwu Udeh; Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, Dr Bernard Doro; Education, Dr Tunji Alausa; Solid Minerals Development, Chief Dele Alake; Women Affairs, Hajiya Imaan Sulaiman-Ibrahim, Minister of State for Budget and Economic Planning, Dr Doris Uzoka-Anite; Minister of State, FCT, Dr Mariya Bunkure, Nigeria’s Permanent Representative to the UN, Amb. Jimoh Ibrahim; Nigeria’s Ambassador to Washington, Amb. Kayode Are, and heads of government agencies as well as top officials of the Nigerian mission in the US, among others. items.title: No nation can reach full potential without gender inclusion — Bamidele
items.description: Describes inclusion as strategic investment, not favour Says inclusion goes beyond women’s presence in institutions By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Leader of the Senate, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele, APC, Ekiti Central, has said no nation can meaningfully realise its full potential when a significant proportion of its population is unable to contribute fully to governance, diplomacy, economic development and public leadership. Bamidele said the inclusion of women in public governance and leadership should not be regarded as an act of favour, but as a strategic investment in Nigeria’s human capital and institutional strength. He spoke on Thursday at the presentation of the book, The Female Diplomat: Navigating Power, Ambition and Identity, held at Nigeria House in New York, United States. The event brought together the Deputy Secretary-General of the United Nations, Ms Amina Mohammed; Minister of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu; Nigeria’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Jimoh Ibrahim; Nigeria’s Ambassador to the United States, Ambassador Kayode Are; and the President/CEO of Montefiore Einstein, among other dignitaries. In a statement issued by the Senate Leader’s Directorate of Media and Public Affairs, Bamidele said Nigeria’s democracy could only be strengthened when citizens were adequately represented in the institutions established to serve them. He said the administration of President Bola Tinubu had recognised, through the Renewed Hope Agenda, the need to harness the abilities and contributions of all Nigerians, including women and young people. Bamidele, who chaired the book presentation, stressed that meaningful inclusion went beyond having women occupy positions in institutions. He said it required genuine opportunities for women to participate in decision-making, exercise responsibility and contribute to the formulation and implementation of public policies. “Gender inclusion is not an act of favour. It is a strategic investment in Nigeria’s human capital and institutional strength. “No nation can realise its full potential if a significant proportion of its population is unable to contribute fully to governance, diplomacy, economic development and public leadership,” he said. The Senate Leader said Nigeria’s democratic institutions would be strengthened when citizens saw themselves represented in institutions established to serve them. He added that the country’s foreign relations would also benefit when Nigeria was represented by capable professionals whose knowledge, judgment and experience reflected the breadth of the country’s talent. Bamidele highlighted the role of the National Assembly in promoting gender inclusion through legislation, representation and oversight. He said the parliament would continue to support institutions that were fair, accessible and responsive, while creating an environment where competence was recognised and qualified women had greater opportunities to contribute to leadership. “This is not a responsibility for the government alone. Political institutions, the diplomatic service, the private sector, academic institutions and civil society all have roles to play. “Progress will require deliberate policies, supportive institutions and a collective willingness to recognise talent wherever it is found,” he said. Bamidele also participated in the Nigeria Investment Forum 2026, which brought together government representatives, international investors, development finance institutions, multinational corporations, business leaders and other stakeholders to explore investment opportunities in Nigeria. He said the book presentation contributed to the broader national conversation on Nigeria’s development and its engagement with the international community. items.title: Deepfakes: INEC chairman tasks editors on fact-checking
items.description: … Cautions media against unofficial results … Says journalists’ welfare critical to democracy By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe ENUGU — The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has urged editors and newsroom managers to strengthen fact-checking and digital verification mechanisms to counter the growing threat of artificial intelligence-driven deepfakes ahead of the 2027 general elections. INEC warned that synthetic disinformation, including manipulated videos, cloned voices and fabricated election result sheets, could undermine public confidence in the electoral process and create confusion during elections. INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, SAN, gave the warning on Thursday at the 22nd All Nigeria Editors Conference (ANEC 2026) in Enugu. Amupitan, who was represented by the Resident Electoral Commissioner for Enugu State, Dr Chukwuemeka Chukwu, spoke on the theme: “The Ballot, the Media and the Task of Keeping Democracy Alive.” In a statement signed by Adedayo Oketola, Chief Press Secretary and Media Adviser to the INEC Chairman, the commission said technological advances had transformed the disinformation landscape, enabling malicious actors to produce convincing audio-visual materials capable of misleading large audiences within a short period. Amupitan said: “We have moved far beyond simple political bias, hyperbole, or unverified rumours into an era of synthetically manufactured reality. “Generative artificial intelligence, voice cloning, deepfake video synthesis, and automated bot networks have democratised mass deception.” He said political actors or other malicious users could produce seemingly authentic videos of electoral officials declaring fictitious results, clone the voices of officials and circulate fabricated result sheets to create the impression of electoral fraud. According to him, the danger posed by deepfakes extends beyond individual falsehoods to the erosion of public trust in genuine information released by constitutional authorities. “When deepfakes render lies believable, real truth is greeted with skepticism. Cynicism replaces civic engagement,” he said. To address the threat, the INEC chairman urged media organisations to establish specialised fact-checking desks, deploy digital verification and forensic tools, and authenticate election-related information before publication. He also urged editors to train journalists to identify synthetic content, fake official documents, manipulated videos and other forms of digitally generated misinformation. No Unofficial Results Amupitan cautioned media organisations against publishing or amplifying privately collated election results before official declarations by INEC. He said premature publication of unofficial figures could create competing narratives, confuse voters and undermine confidence in officially declared results. “Let’s resist premature result declarations. Under the Electoral Act, statutory authority to declare election results rests exclusively with INEC,” he said. He urged editors to ensure that their platforms did not become channels for disseminating unverified election figures generated by political actors or circulated on social media. “The pressure on modern newsrooms to be first is immense. But in national elections, it is vastly more important to be right than to be first,” he said. Amupitan said publishing unverified result sheets, doctored videos or unconfirmed statements could give credibility to deliberate deception and potentially threaten public peace. He called on the Nigerian Guild of Editors and media organisations to develop a collaborative mechanism for identifying and responding rapidly to election-related disinformation. INEC Deploys AI Tools On the commission’s preparations for the 2027 elections, Amupitan said INEC had moved towards a more proactive use of technology. He disclosed that the commission had established an Artificial Intelligence Division within its ICT Department and commenced the deployment of automated AI auditing tools in the results management process. According to him, the tools are designed to detect discrepancies before final verification, while automated checks remain subject to human oversight under a five-pillar AI Governance Framework. He also said the commission had commenced a six-zone Interactive Meetings and Readiness Assessment tour, beginning in Lagos on September 7, to assess electoral preparedness across the country. Amupitan said elections were no longer contested only at polling units but also in the information space, making the media an important partner in safeguarding electoral integrity. Journalists’ Welfare The INEC chairman also highlighted the economic conditions of journalists, arguing that the welfare of media workers was linked to the quality and independence of journalism. He urged media owners and managers to provide decent remuneration and structured welfare packages for journalists, warning that severe financial insecurity could expose media practitioners to inducement and other pressures. “A poorly compensated journalist is vulnerable; a financially neglected newsroom is fertile ground for compromise,” he said. Amupitan said journalists with decent working conditions would be better positioned to resist inducement, scrutinise false narratives and report elections objectively. He added that INEC had introduced measures to improve the welfare of its workforce, including the Consolidated Election Management Body Salary Structure (CEMBSS), which, according to him, separated the commission’s workforce from the regular Civil Service salary structure with effect from January 1, 2026. Editors, Traditional Rulers Seek Stronger Response Earlier, President of the Nigerian Guild of Editors, NGE, Mr Eze Anaba, said the media had a responsibility to protect democracy by holding power accountable and providing platforms for diverse voices. “We have a responsibility to ensure that our democracy survives. The media must hold power accountable and provide the space for diverse voices to be heard,” Anaba said. The Obi of Onitsha, Igwe Nnaemeka Alfred Achebe, urged INEC to establish a joint rapid-response mechanism involving newsrooms to counter election misinformation and provide timely clarification of false claims. Achebe also challenged editors to intensify voter education and address voter apathy by informing citizens about the importance of participating in the electoral process. Speaking on the role of the media in democracy, the Archbishop Emeritus of Abuja, John Cardinal Onaiyekan, said a free press remained essential to democratic governance. Onaiyekan noted that Nigeria had a diverse media landscape comprising newspapers, radio and television stations, as well as social media platforms. He, however, said the emergence of artificial intelligence had introduced both opportunities and risks into the communication space. “Artificial intelligence, AI, is already working wonders in the communication space, though not without its dangers if it is allowed to spin out of human control,” he said. The post Deepfakes: INEC chairman tasks editors on fact-checking appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Phosphate : l’Algérie lance le chantier du complexe géant d’engrais de Souk Ahras
items.description: Après le fer de Gara Djebilet et le zinc-plomb de Béjaïa, l’Algérie lance le projet d'exploitation d’une autre ressource minière stratégique : le phosphate . Le projet intégré d'exploitation du gisement de phosphate de l’est du pays entre dans une phase décisive. Il est officiellement lancé ce jeudi 24 septembre avec la pose de première pierre du chantier de réalisation du complexe de transformation chimique du phosphate de Oued El-Kebir, dans la wilaya de Souk Ahras. La capacité de production du complexe est de 2,4 millions de tonnes par an d’engrais phosphatés et 570 000 tonnes d’engrais azotés. Les travaux seront réalisés par la société italienne Saipem. Le projet comprend l'exploitation du gisement de Tébessa, la réalisation d'un complexe de transformation et d'une ligne de chemin de fer jusqu'au port d'Annaba où un quai minier est en réalisation. Algérie : le projet phosphate intégré franchit une nouvelle étape Deux ministres ont fait le déplacement pour la circonstance, celui des Mines et des Industries minières, Mourad Hanafi, et son collègue des Travaux publics et des Infrastructures de base, Abdelkader Djelaoui, en plus du wali de Souk Ahras et du PDG de Sonatrach. Le complexe constitue le maillon industriel essentiel de la chaîne de valeur du projet intégré du phosphate, indique le ministère des Hydrocarbures dans un communiqué. Les travaux de réalisation sont confiés à la société italienne Saipem selon le modèle de réalisation accélérée “ EPC Fast Track ” dans le but de réduire les délais de réalisation et de respecter le calendrier prévu, ajoute la même source. La réalisation sera exécutée conjointement avec plusieurs filières de Sonatrach, à savoir la Société algérienne de réalisation de projets industriels (SARPI), la Société nationale d’ingénierie civile et de construction (GCB) et l’entreprise des Grands travaux pétroliers (GTP). Plusieurs unités de production de différents types d'engrais Dans une présentation faite sur place, il a été indiqué que le complexe est composé de plusieurs unités industrielles de production d’engrais phosphatés de différents types (le DAP, le MAP et le NPK) ainsi que des engrais azotés, en particulier l’urée, et des produits chimiques intermédiaires, tels que l’acide sulfurique, l’acide phosphorique et l’ammoniac. Toujours selon les mêmes explications, la capacité de production annuelle du complexe sera, dans une première phase, de 2,4 millions de tonnes d'engrais phosphatés, 570 000 tonnes d'engrais azotés, en plus de la production de produits chimiques intermédiaires nécessaires au processus de transformation. L’article Phosphate : l’Algérie lance le chantier du complexe géant d’engrais de Souk Ahras est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Truck crushes okada passenger on Oshodi-Apapa Expressway
items.description: By Ogochukw Agha A yet-to-be-identified adult male passenger on a motorcycle was killed, on Wednesday, after a sand-laden tipper truck collided with the motorcycle at Ilasa Bus Stop, inward Mile 2, on the Oshodi/ Apapa expressway, Lagos. The Lagos State Emergency Management Agency, LASEMA, said its Eagle Response Team stationed at Cappa responded to the crash following a distress call received at about 3:18 p.m. According to the agency’s Permanent Secretary, Dr. Olufemi Oke-Osanyintolu,” Upon arrival, the team discovered that the accident involved a tipper truck loaded with sand, with registration number 19F 992FG, and a motorcycle at the aforementioned location. Preliminary investigation revealed that the incident was caused by reckless driving as the tipper driver lost control of the vehicle and collided with the motorcycle from behind. “Tragically, an adult male passenger on the motorcycle lost his life as a result of the collision. “In line with established emergency response protocols, the LASEMA Response Team, in collaboration with the LRU Paramedics, officials of the Lagos State Traffic Management Authority, LASTMA, and officers of the Nigeria Police Force, who were all present at the scene, professionally managed the situation. The remains of the deceased were recovered, bagged with dignity by the Agency’s responders, and handed over to family members present at the scene in accordance with best practices. “For safety and to prevent further gridlock, the affected tipper truck and motorcycle were subsequently moved off the carriageway and taken to Ilasamaja Police Station for further investigation. “The operation has been concluded and all responders have returned to base while normal traffic flow has been restored in the area.” The Permanent Secretary commiserated with the family of the deceased and appealed to motorists, particularly drivers of articulated vehicles, to exercise caution, observe traffic regulations and avoid reckless driving, in order to prevent avoidable loss of lives on the road. He reiterated the commitment of the Lagos State Government to protecting lives and property through rapid emergency response across the state. items.title: ONU : Mamadi Doumbouya dénonce les « putschistes en costume »
items.description: À la tribune de l’Assemblée générale des Nations unies, mercredi 23 septembre 2026, le président guinéen Mamadi Doumbouya a vivement critiqué les dirigeants qui, selon lui, « tripatouillent » les constitutions en cours de mandat pour se maintenir au pouvoir. Pour le chef de l’État guinéen, le putsch ne se résume pas à une prise de pouvoir par les armes. Il peut également prendre une forme institutionnelle lorsque des dirigeants modifient les règles du jeu politique alors que la partie est déjà engagée. « Le vrai putschiste, c’est celui qui change les règles du jeu pendant la partie », a-t-il déclaré. Mamadi Doumbouya a ainsi dénoncé ceux qu’il présente comme des « putschistes en costume ». Selon lui, ces dirigeants ne renversent pas nécessairement les institutions par la force. Ils procèdent plutôt par « manigance » et « fourberie », en modifiant les règles constitutionnelles afin de préserver leur position au pouvoir. Le président guinéen estime que ces pratiques sont particulièrement répandues sur le continent. Ces « putschistes en costume », a-t-il affirmé, seraient « les plus nombreux » et ne feraient l’objet d’« aucune condamnation ». Dans son propos, Mamadi Doumbouya a également établi un lien entre les crises politiques africaines et plusieurs facteurs qu’il considère comme déterminants : les promesses non tenues, « l’endormissement du peuple » et le « tripatouillage des constitutions ». À ses yeux, le respect des règles institutionnelles constitue ainsi un élément essentiel de la stabilité politique. Changer les règles en cours de partie revient, selon son argumentaire, à rompre l’équilibre institutionnel, même lorsque cette modification intervient dans un cadre qui se présente comme légal. items.title: Influenceurs, TikTokeurs…: «Vous n’êtes pas des journalistes…»
items.description: La directrice des affaires juridiques et du contentieux de la Haute autorité de régulation de la communication écrite, audiovisuelle et numérique (HARC) au Togo, N’do Pabozi, a recadré les acteurs des médias sociaux en déclarant: «Vous n’êtes pas des journalistes, vous ne sortez pas d’une école de formation en journalisme», au cours d'une rencontre le mardi 22 septembre 2026 à Lomé. La Haute autorité de régulation de la communication écrite, audiovisuelle et numérique (HARC) entend désormais renforcer son regard sur les nouveaux acteurs de l’information en ligne. Réunis mardi 22 septembre 2026 à Lomé, blogueurs, influenceurs, youtubeurs, TikTokeurs et autres créateurs de contenus, ont été sensibilisés sur leurs responsabilités dans un espace numérique devenu incontournable dans la circulation de l’information, rapporte Ledefenseurinfo. Première du genre depuis l’élargissement des missions de la HARC à la communication numérique par la Constitution du 6 mai 2024, cette rencontre marque une nouvelle étape dans l’encadrement des pratiques sur les réseaux sociaux. Le président de la HARC, Pitalounani Télou, a pour sa part souligné que le nouveau mandat de l’institution englobe désormais «l’espace occupé par les influenceurs, blogueurs, tiktokeurs, web-activistes et administrateurs de plateformes numériques». Cette approche vise un meilleur encadrement des pratiques sur les réseaux sociaux. Avec l’essor des plateformes numériques au Togo, les réseaux sociaux sont devenus un important canal de diffusion de l’information. Mais cette évolution s’accompagne de risques liés aux fausses informations, aux rumeurs, au harcèlement, aux discours de haine et aux atteintes à la dignité. A l'issue de cette rencontre, les participants sont appelés à s'engager pour élaborer un code de bonne conduite et de déontologie, dans une logique d’autorégulation. Par Wakat Séra L’article Influenceurs, TikTokeurs…: «Vous n’êtes pas des journalistes…» est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Retirement security begins on the job, not at retirement — Faleye
items.description: —Says NSITF now covers 7.8m workers; claim processing time cut to 10 days By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA– THE Managing Director and Chief Executive of the Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF),Oluwaseun Faleye, on Thursday said that individual efforts in retirement planning cannot substitute for institutional responsibility, emphasising that retirement security must be built during one’s working life, not at the point of exit from service. Faleye made the statement while presenting NSITF’s position at the Policy Dialogue session of the 2026 National Pre-Retirement Summit, themed “Own Your Retirement: From Planning to Action,” held at the Shehu Musa Yar’Adua Centre in Abuja. Speaking at the session, themed “Between Duty and Delivery”, the Managing Director said social protection hinges on the gap between what the law promises citizens and what they actually experience. He said, “When we speak about retirement, we must begin much earlier than the point at which work ends. Retirement security is shaped during working life – by occupational risks, health, protection of earning capacity, compensation when harm occurs, and what happens to families when a breadwinner is lost”. He stated that while pensions and savings are indispensable, they do not tell the whole story. The NSITF boss noted that a worker who remains healthy, productive and protected has a different pathway into old age from one who suffers disabling injury or premature death without adequate protection. Faleye explained that the Employees’ Compensation Scheme (ECS), which NSITF administers, is part of the retirement and social protection continuum, protecting workers against employment-related injury, occupational disease, disability and death, while providing compensation, survivor protection, medical care, rehabilitation and return-to-work support. On coverage, the NSITF boss disclosed that as at July 2026, more than 7.6 million workers were enrolled under the Scheme, adding that current figure has risen to over 7.8 million. He said the Fund is moving from isolated registration exercises toward sustained participation and compliance through partnerships with Federal institutions, State Governments,regulators, employers and organisations in the informal economy. He described the onboarding of Treasury-funded Federal MDAs as particularly significant, revealing that within less than four months of the integration process, claims payments have commenced. “The first batch of five Treasury-funded MDA beneficiaries was paid on 4 August 2026. This is turning Federal Civil Service protection into a lived reality,” Faleye said. He stressed that registration alone is not protection, adding that compliance must deliver real protection by connecting registration and assessment to contributions, accurate worker information, claims and timely benefit payment. Faleye said the family must remain visible in social protection design, noting that when a worker dies from employment-related incident, survivors’ and dependents’ benefits become critical. “The system must be visible at the point of vulnerability. Claims administration, documentation, communication and inter-agency referrals should be designed around the beneficiary’s experience, with compassion, clarity and timely resolution,” he added. On prevention, he said NSITF’s occupational safety and health work through workplace inspection, accident investigation and safety advocacy is aimed at ensuring fewer accidents occur at workplaces, while healthcare and rehabilitation preserve dignity and earning capacity. The NSITF Chief Executive said workers should plan for retirement and understand their entitlements, but warned that a worker cannot individually insure against an employer’s non-compliance or build a claims system. “The right balance is shared responsibility: the State builds and regulates the architecture; institutions deliver within their mandates; employers comply and maintain safe workplaces; and workers understand, use and participate actively in the protections available to them,” he stated. He listed NSITF’s position as: retirement security begins during working life; coverage must mean effective protection not merely registration; prevention and compensation must work together; families and dependents must remain part of protection design; and individual ownership complements but does not replace public and employer responsibilities. “Between duty and delivery is where trust is won. For the Nigerian worker, social protection must be more than a statutory promise on paper. It must be felt when a worker is injured, when a family loses a breadwinner, when rehabilitation is needed, and when a worker approaches retirement,” Faleye said. He disclosed that average claims turnaround has improved to 10 days from 14 days, adding that the next task is to deepen coverage, strengthen compliance and improve institutional coordination. “A worker can plan for retirement only when the system is credible enough to plan with,” he concluded. items.title: ‘I was sexually assaulted’ — Andy Carroll reveals traumatic incident
items.description: Former Liverpool and England striker Andy Carroll has revealed he was sexually assaulted by a man in 2021. Carroll wrote in his autobiography ‘Owning it’ that the incident took place at his home with a man he had invited to stay over after watching a boxing fight on television. The perpetrator, a friend of Carroll’s former partner, was eventually jailed for three years. The 37-year-old, who is now a player and co-owner of non-league club Dagenham and Redbridge, was automatically granted anonymity as a victim of sexual assault. Carroll said the incident happened when he was sleeping. He threw the man out of the house and knocked him unconscious when he attempted to get back inside. “I was sexually assaulted, there I said it. Scary to even think about and only a few people knew about it before now,” Carroll wrote. Carroll decided to include the incident in his book “at the very last minute” after discussing it with his girlfriend Lou Teasdale. “Me and Lou spent a lot of time discussing whether to mention it in this book or not. I avoided my publisher for so long that they probably suspected I got cold feet,” he wrote. “Scary to talk about but it’s made (me) the person I am today as much as any of the good stuff. And if me talking about it helps just one person then good, it will have been worth it.” Carroll said testifying in court, where the attacker was found guilty of sexual offences and placed on the sex offender register, was “humiliating and embarrassing and absolutely horrendous”. The former Newcastle and West Ham forward, who won nine caps for England, added: “What happened to me affected every facet of my life. “I’d think about it every day, making it difficult to focus on anything else, including football. The trauma of what happened to me hasn’t gone away.” Vanguard News The post ‘I was sexually assaulted’ — Andy Carroll reveals traumatic incident appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Recherche scientifique : Le Réseau des chercheurs Agbajòwò, en partenariat avec l'UCAO-UUB, organise un colloque international sur « Endogénéité et renaissance de l'Afrique »
items.description: Face aux enjeux de souveraineté et d'émancipation intellectuelle du continent, le Réseau des Chercheurs Agbajòwò, en partenariat avec l'Université Catholique de l'Afrique de l'Ouest - Unité universitaire de Bobo-Dioulasso (UCAO-UUB), organise les 26 et 27 novembre 2026 un colloque international d'envergure intitulé : « Endogénéité et renaissance de l'Afrique ». Ce colloque offre un cadre interdisciplinaire inédit visant à dépasser les schémas théoriques conventionnels. Ces réflexions convergent vers une idée centrale : l'Afrique ne peut se contenter d'importer des modèles exogènes de développement. Les questions qui se posent sont donc les suivantes : Comment réhabiliter les savoirs endogènes et les épistémologies africaines pour construire une modernité assumée et souveraine ? Comment l'Afrique peut-elle mobiliser ses savoirs endogènes, ses patrimoines culturels et ses dynamiques sociales pour construire une renaissance durable, tout en dialoguant avec les défis et les opportunités du monde actuel ? Cette rencontre vise à renforcer la conviction que la renaissance africaine ne peut se réaliser qu'à travers une appropriation consciente de ses ressources culturelles, scientifiques et sociales, tout en s'inscrivant dans les dynamiques de la mondialisation. S'inscrivant dans le sillage de grandes figures intellectuelles et décoloniales (P. Hountondji, Ch. A. Diop, K. Nkrumah, F. Sarr, S. B. Diagne), l'événement réunira chercheurs, enseignants-chercheurs, doctorants, étudiants et praticiens du développement pour penser des solutions africaines aux défis contemporains. Les échanges s'articuleront autour de 5 axes majeurs : LES 5 AXES THÉMATIQUES MAJEURS 1. Endogénéité et rationalité : Épistémologies africaines, langues locales, sciences modernes et transformation numérique. 2. Néo-panafricanisme : Mobilisations de la jeunesse, rôle de la diaspora, intégration économique et expressions culturelles. 3. Patrimoine et gouvernance : Institutions traditionnelles, cohésion sociale et politiques publiques inclusives. 4. Guerre, conflits et paix : Mécanismes traditionnels de médiation et solutions africaines aux défis sécuritaires. 5. Spiritualités et religions : Interactions entre religions endogènes et religions du Livre pour la renaissance culturelle. Un carrefour d'échanges scientifiques et d'innovation Placé sous le signe de l'excellence académique et de la coopération interuniversitaire, cet événement scientifique constitue une plateforme privilégiée de partage de connaissances, de présentation de travaux originaux et de création de réseaux de recherche. Durant deux jours, conférences plénières, tables rondes et ateliers thématiques rythmeront la vie du campus. À la date butoir fixée au 15 juillet 2026 pour la soumission des résumés, 85 contributions avaient été enregistrées, témoignant ainsi du vif intérêt suscité par cet événement scientifique et de la forte mobilisation de la communauté académique autour de la thématique du colloque. Cette manifestation scientifique illustre l'engagement du Réseau des Chercheurs Agbajòwò ( "C'est ensemble qu'on est fort") et l' l'UCAO-UUB à promouvoir une recherche de pointe ancrée dans les réalités de nos sociétés, tout en favorisant le rayonnement international de ces deux institutions. Il ne s'agit pas seulement d'un rendez-vous académique, mais d'un moment de réflexion collective où chercheurs, praticiens, décideurs politiques, acteurs de la société civile et représentants des communautés locales pourront confronter leurs expériences et leurs visions. Ce colloque se présente comme une plateforme stratégique pour penser et agir en faveur d'une Afrique qui se réinvente à partir d'elle-même, tout en dialoguant avec le monde. Les hommes de média, le grand public, les acteurs de la société civile et du monde universitaire sont tous invités à prendre part activement à cette agape scientifique, grand rendez-vous du donné et du recevoir du 26 au 27 novembre 2026 à l'Université Catholique de l'Afrique de l'Ouest-Unité universitaire de Bobo-Dioulasso (UCAO-UUB). items.title: Lagos moves to restore order in trucking business
items.description: By Godwin Oritse LAGOS — The Lagos State Government has intensified efforts to restore compliance, safety and orderly operations in the trucking business, particularly along major maritime corridors in the state. The Lagos State Truck and Cargo Operators Committee (LASTCOC) consequently urged truck owners, drivers, terminal operators and other stakeholders in the maritime transport sector to cooperate with the government in implementing the measures. Speaking at a meeting with transport stakeholders in Lagos, the Permanent Secretary, Lagos State Ministry of Transportation, Mr Olawale Musa, examined persistent challenges affecting the movement of trucks and cargo along the state’s maritime corridors. Musa said the government was particularly concerned about avoidable traffic congestion, accidents and loss of lives arising from activities along the corridors. “We want sanity and compliance,” he said. The Permanent Secretary, who chaired the meeting, disclosed that additional personnel and equipment would be deployed to strengthen traffic management and improve operations along the affected corridors. He also clarified that the government’s objective was not to generate revenue from truck operators through fines or other interventions, but to enforce compliance, promote orderly operations and prevent incidents that could result in loss of lives and property. Stakeholders at the meeting also discussed measures to improve cargo evacuation from the ports, noting that delays within the port system directly affect truck turnaround time and contribute to congestion on port access roads. They called for a review of operations along the Lekki-Epe corridor and the call-up system to address emerging traffic challenges and ensure that the system reflects the realities of trucking operations in the area. Participants urged truck operators to comply with approved guidelines rather than resorting to financial interventions when violations or traffic obstructions occur. The Lagos State Government had also warned truck operators along the Lekki corridor against using payments or informal interventions to resolve traffic violations, insisting on compliance with established call-up and traffic management procedures. The Ministry of Transportation urged truck operators to properly organise their activities and follow approved guidelines, stressing that the government’s priority was to restore order and safety rather than generate revenue through fines. In a statement, the Chairman of LASTCOC, Alhaji Lukman Shittu Zangalo, called on truck owners, drivers, terminal operators and other stakeholders to support the measures. He said improved compliance would enhance road safety, facilitate port operations and protect lives and businesses. Stakeholders at the meeting included the Nigerian Port Economic Regulatory Agency (NPERA), Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA), Association of Maritime Truck Owners (AMATO) and LASTCOC. The post Lagos moves to restore order in trucking business appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: US and Iran discuss phased deal to reopen Hormuz and end US blockade, sources say
items.description: By Samia Nakhoul, Parisa Hafezi and John Irish Sept 24 (Reuters) - US and Iranian negotiators in New York are exploring a phased path out of war that would involve Tehran reopening the Strait of Hormuz and Washington lifting its economic blockade of Iran, sources close to the talks said. items.title: Why I started ‘Curiosity Made Me Ask’ after skit-making — Isbae U
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Content creator Adebayo Ridwan Abidemi, popularly known as Isbae U, has revealed how he birthed his popular interview series, Curiosity Made Me Ask, saying he wanted to create something unique and different from skit-making. Isbae U disclosed this during an interview with media personality Morayo Afolabi-Brown on The Morayo Show, shared on YouTube on Wednesday. He said the idea emerged while he was trying to find his identity in the entertainment industry, having previously explored singing, rapping and skit-making. “There was a day I said to someone that I was done being mediocre, being average. I wanted to do something different. I didn’t want to just be considered part of them, part of the skit makers, one of them,” he said. Isbae U said American comedian Zach Galifianakis’ interview show, Between Two Ferns, later inspired the concept. “I saw a show that I used to watch a long time ago. It’s called Between Two Ferns by Zach Galifianakis. So when I saw the show, I loved it. I thought, ‘Oh, this is something I can do,’” he said. According to him, the idea behind Curiosity Made Me Ask is to reveal a side of celebrities that audiences do not usually see. “The idea of Curiosity Made Me Ask is to show you another part of this celebrity you’ve not seen,” he said. The show has since featured prominent personalities, including former President Olusegun Obasanjo and veteran actor Pete Edochie. Isbae U also dismissed the perception that he had abandoned skit-making for the interview series, saying he still works behind the scenes. “A lot of people thought or think I have stopped creating and just doing Curiosity Made Me Ask. But low-key, there are people I write stories for, people I help with their stories,” he said. items.description: El presidente de Ceuta, Juan Jesús Vivas , ha rebajado su discurso respecto a los menores extranjeros no acompañados llegados a la ciudad autónoma en el cruce masivo. items.title: Police seal suspected fake wine factory in Lagos
items.description: By Stanley Umejiaku LAGOS — Operatives of the Lagos State Police Command have uncovered and sealed a suspected illegal factory allegedly used to produce and package adulterated alcoholic drinks in the Yafin area of Badagry, Lagos State. The operation also led to the arrest of a 48-year-old man identified as Anaebo Hilary, who was found at the premises. The Police Public Relations Officer in the state, SP Abimbola Adebisi, who confirmed the development, said the operation followed credible intelligence provided by members of the public. According to her, operatives recovered adulterated alcoholic drinks, empty bottles, different wine labels and various production utensils suspected to have been used in producing and packaging the drinks. She said the factory was subsequently sealed, while the suspect was taken into police custody for further investigation. “The recovered items have been taken to the station for further investigation,” Adebisi said. The Commissioner of Police, Lagos State Command, CP Tijani Fatai, commended the operatives for their vigilance and prompt response to the information. He reaffirmed the command’s commitment to sustaining intelligence-led operations against criminal activities across the state. The CP also urged members of the public to continue providing timely and credible information to the police through the command’s emergency lines: 07061019374, 08065154338, 08063299264, 08039344870, 08080193432 (Marine), and 09168630929. items.title: Législatives : après sa victoire, le PAM tend la main aux autres forces politiques
items.description: Au lendemain de sa victoire aux élections législatives, le Parti Authenticité et Modernité (PAM) veut désormais tourner la page de la compétition électorale pour se consacrer à l’action publique. Arrivé en tête du scrutin avec 97 sièges, le parti du tracteur affirme que la confiance exprimée par les électeurs constitue avant tout une « responsabilité nationale ». Le message a été porté ce jeudi à Rabat par Fatima Saâdi, membre de la direction collégiale du PAM, qui a donné lecture d’un communiqué de la formation lors d’une conférence de presse tenue au lendemain du scrutin. Le parti y exprime sa reconnaissance aux électrices et aux électeurs qui lui ont accordé leurs voix, tout en adressant ses remerciements à ses militants, candidats et équipes mobilisées pendant la campagne. Le PAM insiste notamment sur le travail de terrain et la proximité avec les citoyens, qu’il présente comme deux des facteurs ayant contribué à son résultat. La direction du parti a également salué les différentes formations politiques marocaines pour « l’esprit de compétition, de citoyenneté et de démocratie » ayant marqué la campagne électorale, ainsi que les autorités et les institutions ayant assuré l’organisation du scrutin. Une victoire présentée comme une responsabilité Pour le PAM, les 97 sièges obtenus ne constituent pas seulement un résultat électoral. La formation assure vouloir répondre à la confiance qui lui a été accordée en plaçant au premier plan « l’intérêt général du pays et la dignité des Marocains », notamment dans leur vie quotidienne, leur santé, leur emploi, leur éducation et l’avenir de leurs enfants. Le parti insiste sur un point : son action devra concerner l’ensemble des Marocains, « ceux qui ont voté pour nous comme ceux qui n’ont pas voté pour nous ». Une manière, dans son communiqué, de marquer la fin de la confrontation électorale et de placer la prochaine étape sous le signe du travail collectif. Le PAM revendique par ailleurs son résultat comme une reconnaissance de son action et des efforts consentis au cours des dernières années. Mais il souligne dans le même temps que la participation à la gestion des affaires publiques implique des responsabilités et impose d’assumer les conséquences des choix politiques. « Nous tournons la page de la compétition » Le parti entend surtout changer de registre après la campagne électorale. « Nous tournons maintenant la page de la compétition électorale pour nous diriger tous vers le service de notre pays », affirme-t-on dans le communiqué. Dans cette perspective, le PAM dit croire à « la propreté du travail politique », au travail commun et à une « main tendue » au service de l’intérêt du pays. Il appelle ainsi à la coopération entre les différentes forces et composantes de la scène politique pour faire face aux défis auxquels le Maroc sera confronté durant la prochaine période. La formation évoque à ce titre de « grandes échéances » qui nécessitent, selon elle, une mobilisation collective. Le mot d’ordre avancé par le parti pour la période qui s’ouvre est donc celui de la mobilisation « pour la patrie et pour l’intérêt des Marocains ». Avec 97 sièges, le PAM arrive en tête des résultats provisoires des législatives du 23 septembre, devant le RNI avec 66 sièges et l’Istiqlal avec 65. Le scrutin a enregistré une participation nationale de 38,02%. The post Législatives : après sa victoire, le PAM tend la main aux autres forces politiques appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Kpendjal-Ouest/Journée internationale de la paix : Des débats sur la paix et la cohésion sociale menés à Naki-est
items.description: Naki-Est, 24 sept. (ATOP) – La journée internationale de la paix a été célébrée en différé le mercredi 23 septembre à Naki-Est sur le thème « Investir dans la paix pour tous, partout, chaque jour ». La célébration s’intègre dans le projet « Action intégrée de réponse de crise dans la région des Savanes au Togo (Savanes Kpaadu) », mis en œuvre par Plan International Togo et ses partenaires, avec le financement de l’Union européenne (UE). Elle vise à renforcer la mobilisation citoyenne et le dialogue entre les communautés, tout en contribuant à la promotion de la paix, de la cohésion sociale et du vivre-ensemble. Le préfet de Kpendjal-Ouest lors de son discours Vue partielle de l’assistance L’événement a été marquée par un forum communautaire, des échanges avec les jeunes et les organisations de la société civile, ainsi que des animations socioculturelles. Le projet « Savanes Kpaadu », ses objectifs et ses actions, ainsi que les opportunités d’entrepreneuriat ont été présentés aux communautés. Celles-ci ont été en outre sensibilisées sur le vivre-ensemble, la paix et la cohésion sociale. Le préfet de Kpendjal-Ouest, Col. Bakaï Pidassa a souligné que la paix et le vivre-ensemble constituent un levier essentiel pour le développement durable. Il a invité la population à œuvrer pour contribuer à l’enracinement de la paix dans la localité. Le maire de Kpendjal-Ouest 1, Mme Didjengou Fékandine a émis le vœu que cette initiative favorise une prise de conscience collective sur l’importance de la cohésion sociale, du vivre-ensemble et la fraternité entre les communautés. La coordinatrice de Plan International Togo, bureau Savanes et Kara, Mme Abalo Naka a précisé qu’à travers ces assises, sa structure entend transformer ces occasions symboliques en véritables plateformes de mobilisation populaire, capables de renforcer le vivre-ensemble et de contrecarrer les discours de division et de haine. La journée internationale de la paix est observée chaque 21 septembre. ATOP/BLS/JK/BV

items.title: “No Nation is Inferior”: Mahama champions human dignity and security council reform at the UN
items.description: Addressing the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York on September 24, 2026, Ghanaian President His Excellency John Dramani Mahama delivered an expansive speech calling for systemic international reform, global justice, and a renewed commitment to human dignity. Speaking from a podium historically graced by Pan-African leaders, President Mahama challenged the assembly to confront historical atrocities, restructure global governance and finance, address environmental degradation, and recognise the shared humanity of all global citizens. Roots, Identity, and the Concept of Belonging President Mahama opened his address by drawing upon Ghana’s national anthem, highlighting its call to be bold in defending the cause of freedom and right while cherishing fearless honesty. He reflected on his personal origins in Damongo, capital of the Savannah Region, describing his heritage as a reflection of Ghana’s rich cultural tapestry. Highlighting his ability to speak several languages, including Gonja, Akan, Ga, Hausa, English, and a working understanding of Ewe, he noted that language creates genuine kinship among diverse peoples. While acknowledging that belonging serves as a vital source of dignity and pride, Mahama cautioned against its weaponisation into nativism, chauvinism, xenophobia, and prejudice. He re-anchored his address in the founding principle of the United Nations, reminding world leaders that every human being belongs to the human family regardless of race, faith, language, or origin. Historic Acknowledgment, Resolution A/RES/80/250, and Reparatory Justice A central theme of the address was the pursuit of full international recognition and repair for historic atrocities. President Mahama highlighted the passage of Resolution A/RES/80/250 on March 25, 2026, marking the International Day of Remembrance of the Victims of Slavery and the Transatlantic Slave Trade. Tabled by Ghana and supported by 123 nations, the resolution formally affirmed that the transatlantic slave trade and chattel enslavement were the gravest crimes against humanity in human history. Mahama acknowledged positive moves by countries such as the Netherlands, Germany, and France to join conversations on reparatory justice and restitution. However, the President emphasised that true repair extends beyond gestures and requires dismantling exploitative structures, including unfair global trade regimes, predatory resource extraction, discriminatory credit ratings, unsustainable debt burdens, and the continuous export of raw materials without local value addition. Demands for Systemic Global Reform President Mahama outlined significant disparities in current global governance and financial systems. Highlighting that Africa represents over 18 percent of humanity with 1.5 billion people and constitutes the largest regional voting bloc in the General Assembly, Mahama demanded permanent African representation on the UN Security Council with full veto powers, arguing that current structures reflect outdated post-war geopolitical realities. He criticized lending practices that force developing nations to borrow at interest rates up to eight times higher than industrialized nations, forcing governments into a tragic choice between servicing predatory debt or serving their populations. Rejecting any new scramble for Africa, Mahama declared that critical minerals required for the global green transition must be processed within the continent to build local industries, create jobs, and retain value. He pointed to the African Continental Free Trade Area, headquartered in Accra, as the primary engine for intra-African trade and structural industrialization. Conflict, Multilateralism, and International Law Reiterating that the UN Charter must prevail over unilateralism and the doctrine that might makes right, Mahama addressed several ongoing global security crises. In Gaza, he called for an immediate end to human carnage, collective punishment, enforced starvation, and mass displacement. He reaffirmed Ghana’s recognition of the sovereign State of Palestine and support for a Two-State solution, while explicitly condemning acts of terrorism by Hamas. Regarding Sudan, cited as the world’s worst humanitarian crisis, he urged elevated global solidarity, while also pledging support for nations combating terrorism, particularly the Alliance of Sahel States. Furthermore, Mahama reiterated calls for an immediate lifting of the decades-long economic, commercial, and financial embargo imposed on Cuba. Across all global disputes, he insisted on a uniform standard of respect for sovereign integrity, protection of civilians, unhindered humanitarian access, and accountability for war crimes. Climate Justice and Global Health Security On environmental issues, President Mahama noted that while Africa contributes less than 4 percent of global greenhouse gas emissions, it suffers disproportionately from climate devastation. He cited a severe event on June 29, 2026, when coastal West Africa and Ghana experienced over 160 millimeters of torrential rainfall within 24 hours across seven regions, resulting in 39 deaths. He demanded that developed nations fulfill climate finance commitments through predictable, non-debt-creating grants rather than loans. In global health, Mahama advocated for the implementation of the Accra Reset, demanding regional manufacturing of vaccines and therapeutics, stronger epidemic surveillance, and resilient public health infrastructure throughout the Global South. Domestic Renewal: The Resetting Ghana Agenda Turning to domestic governance, President Mahama stressed that African leaders must govern with transparency, fight corruption, and ensure accountability. He outlined key domestic initiatives under his administration, describing macroeconomic stabilization measures as a Ghanaian miracle validated by international financial institutions and rating agencies through restored growth, reduced inflation, a stabilized national currency, and lowered public debt. He detailed major infrastructure and industrial initiatives, including the Big Push Programme, the 24-Hour Economy and Accelerated Export Development Programme, and the New Ghana, New Economy policy aimed at driving round-the-clock commercial operations and industrial growth. In social protection, Ghana officially launched a Free Primary Health Care Programme offering community-level care at zero cost, alongside the National Health Insurance Scheme and the specialized Ghana Medical Trust Fund, popularly known as MahamaCare, which subsidizes treatment for Non-Communicable Diseases like renal failure, cancer, cardiovascular diseases, and diabetes. Future Horizons: Looking to 2027 President Mahama concluded by highlighting two major milestones ahead for Ghana. In March 2027, Ghana will celebrate its 70th Anniversary of Independence as the first sub-Saharan African nation to break colonial rule, and in January 2027, Ghana will assume the Chairmanship of the African Union. Mahama pledged to use the AU Chairmanship to drive continental integration, accelerate the AfCFTA, promote peace, and ensure that Africa speaks with a unified voice on the global stage. Expanding on Kwame Nkrumah’s historic 1957 declaration, Mahama concluded that the freedom, prosperity, and peace of any single nation remain insecure unless linked to the total liberation and shared justice of all humanity.

items.title: 2027: Hardship unbearable, deny Tinubu second term — Atiku
items.description: ADC will take over — Aregbesola, as Jegede defects By Dayo Johnson, Akure AKURE — Former Vice President and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has urged Nigerians to reject President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in the 2027 general elections, saying the hardship in the country has become unbearable. Atiku spoke on Thursday in Akure, Ondo State, during the official reception for former two-time governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Eyitayo Jegede, SAN, who formally joined the ADC alongside his supporters. The former Vice President accused the All Progressives Congress (APC) administration of failing to deliver the dividends of democracy and urged Nigerians to vote the party out in 2027. “We are committed to restoring subsidy, we are committed to restoring security all over this country. If we are elected, no part of this country will feel insecure anymore,” Atiku said. He recalled what he described as the economic gains recorded between 1999 and 2007, when he served as vice president, and argued that Nigeria’s economic position had deteriorated under the APC. “You know what we did between 1999 and 2007, we made Nigeria the finest economy in Africa. Today we are number five. Who is responsible for taking us backward? Is it not the APC? This is the moment to vote them out,” he said. Atiku said calls for political change were growing across the country, adding: “There is this popular saying now that Tinubu must go.” He cited the recent Osun governorship election as an example of voter participation and vigilance, urging ADC supporters to replicate such mobilisation in 2027. “I appeal to those who have voter cards, for their own sake, their families and their future, to go out and vote. That is the solution to the problems they are facing. After voting, they should stay, escort and ensure that those votes are counted,” he said. Welcoming Jegede into the ADC, Atiku described his defection as a boost to the party’s preparations for 2027. “You can see our brother and friend Eyitayo and his associates have joined us today. We are winning the coming presidential election,” he said. ADC Will Take Over Representing ADC National Chairman, Senator David Mark, at the event, the party’s National Secretary, Rauf Aregbesola, said the party would mobilise to win the 2027 elections. “We are going to let everyone know that ADC is the boss when we vote in January and February. We are going to mobilise to win the coming election. You can see things are costly, we are going to bring the cost down,” Aregbesola said. He said the strength of the party would ultimately be determined by votes, urging supporters to mobilise voters and ensure their mandates were protected. Aregbesola also said the ADC was committed to a credible electoral process in which votes would count and mandates freely given by voters would be respected without fear or intimidation. Jegede: Suffering Too Much In his remarks, Jegede decried rising unemployment and economic hardship, saying the situation required a change in government. “There is unemployment in Nigeria, you can all see that. There is hardship, you can all see that. The suffering is too much,” he said. Jegede said his defection marked the beginning of a new political journey, expressing confidence that the ADC would make significant gains in the 2027 elections. “The journey has begun. We want a democratic government. We are sure of winning the Senate, House of Representatives and the Presidency. We are going to mobilise and unite to win in 2027. All PDP members loyal to me have moved to ADC,” he said. The Ondo State Chairman of the ADC, Tola Alabere, in his vote of thanks, welcomed Jegede and his supporters, expressing confidence that the party would make significant gains in the state and across the country. Jegede Raises Venue Withdrawal Claim Meanwhile, Jegede raised concern over the alleged last-minute withdrawal of the approved venue for the reception. Through the organising committee, he alleged that the NEPA Car Park in Akure, which had been approved and paid for, was withdrawn by the state government a few hours before the event. He said the development disrupted arrangements for the reception but commended his supporters for remaining peaceful and accepting an alternative venue without confrontation. The ADC has been positioning itself as a platform for opposition realignment ahead of the 2027 elections, with Jegede’s formal entry adding to its growing political activity in Ondo State. The post 2027: Hardship unbearable, deny Tinubu second term — Atiku appeared first on Vanguard News .

L’entretien sera diffusé aujourd’hui à 18h 10 sur france24. Au cours de cet échange, le Président Bassirou Diomaye Faye revient « sur l’accord avec le FMI et la situation économique du pays, mais aussi sur la situation politique nationale, l’éventualité d’une dissolution de l’Assemblée nationale et le calendrier des élections locales », informe les services de communication du groupe RFI et france24. CHRICED demands probe into Wike’s G5 claim on 2023 poll
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The Resource Centre for Human Rights and Civic Education, CHRICED, has demanded an investigation into Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike’s claim that the G5 governors deliberately allowed Labour Party presidential candidate, Peter Obi, to win in parts of the South-South during the 2023 presidential election to weaken the chances of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, candidate, Atiku Abubakar. The group said the claim raised serious questions about the role of powerful political actors in shaping electoral outcomes and the extent to which voters’ choices may have been influenced during the 2023 presidential poll. In a statement on Thursday, CHRICED’s Executive Director, Comrade Dr Ibrahim M. Zikirullahi, called for clarification from the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, the National Assembly, the Attorney-General of the Federation and relevant security agencies. Wike had said on a television programme that the G5 governors considered Atiku and the PDP a greater threat in the South-South and therefore allowed Obi to win in states including Edo and Cross River, while ensuring he did not win Rivers because of the political implications. “It was only Rivers that said, ‘No, we have a problem here in Rivers. Obi will not win here. If he wins, it sends a signal somewhere, people may not understand it.’ And we stopped it,” Wike said. CHRICED said the disclosure should not be dismissed as political banter, arguing that any deliberate effort by political actors to influence electoral outcomes would raise questions about voter sovereignty and the integrity of the electoral process. “If state officials can ‘allow’ or ‘prevent’ candidates from winning in their states, then the fundamental principle that sovereignty belongs to the people is gravely undermined,” the organisation said. The group asked Wike and the other former G5 governors; Seyi Makinde, Samuel Ortom, Okezie Ikpeazu and Ifeanyi Ugwuanyi, to explain the nature, extent and mechanisms of the strategy. It also called for an inquiry into whether any actions by state officials compromised the 2023 presidential election, while demanding stronger safeguards against political interference ahead of the 2027 elections. “Elections are not chessboards for powerful individuals to manipulate at will. They are solemn civic exercises through which citizens express their democratic will,” CHRICED said. The organisation further urged INEC, civil society groups and the media to intensify voter education ahead of 2027, particularly on voting, counting, collation and declaration of results. It said the controversy should prompt renewed efforts to strengthen public confidence in elections, stressing that the ballot belongs to the people. items.title: Soupçonné de trafic de stupéfiants, un Nigérian a été interpellé
items.description: La Gendarmerie nationale du Sénégal a annoncé, ce jeudi 24 septembre 2026, l’interpellation d’un ressortissant nigérian soupçonné d’être impliqué dans un trafic de stupéfiants à Liberté 6, à Dakar. Une opération menée par le Groupe de lutte anti-drogue (GLAD) a, notamment, permis de saisir de la cocaïne, du crack et du chanvre indien. L’opération remonte au lundi 21 septembre 2026. Elle fait suite à un renseignement faisant état de l’existence d’un réseau de trafic de drogue opérant dans le secteur des SICAP Libertés. Sur la base de ces informations, les éléments du Groupe de lutte anti-drogue de la Gendarmerie nationale ont effectué une intervention dans le secteur. Un individu de nationalité nigériane, résidant à Liberté 6, a alors été interpellé. La fouille effectuée sur le suspect a conduit à la découverte de 40 grammes de cocaïne, 25 boules de crack ainsi que du chanvre indien conditionné, selon la Gendarmerie nationale du Sénégal. Cette interpellation intervient dans le cadre des opérations menées par les forces de sécurité sénégalaises contre les réseaux de trafic de stupéfiants. La Gendarmerie nationale poursuit ses investigations afin de faire la lumière sur les activités du suspect et d’éventuelles ramifications du réseau signalé dans le secteur des SICAP Libertés. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Soupçonné de trafic de stupéfiants, un Nigérian a été interpellé est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .
