items.title: ANSACA raises alarm over rising HIV/AIDS cases in Anambra
items.description: By Nwabueze Okonkwo ONITSHA – The Anambra State AIDS Control Agency, ANSACA has raised an alarm over the rising spate of HIV/AIDS scourge in the state. ANSACA, however, expressed optimism that the rising spate of the scourge has not claimed lives as envisaged due to the timely interventions of the Agency through its newly launched telehealth platforms. Executive Director and Project Manager of ANSACA, Dr. Nkem Okeke disclosed this in Awka, while launching a telehealth platform to expand confidential access to HIV prevention, testing, treatment and care, particularly for people facing stigma, distance and gaps in follow-up care. He explained that more than 2,500 people had been tested through community, motor-park, workplace and tertiary-institution outreaches since April, with those requiring additional services linked to appropriate care. According to Okeke, “Testing is not the end. It is the beginning of a pathway to prevention, treatment and sustained care. Healthcare must not be limited by distance.” Also, he unveiled the agency’s maiden newsletter. It links to about 176 primary healthcare centres providing HIV services across the state. Okeke further explained that the newsletter offers information, counselling and referrals for Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP), Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP), HIV testing, treatment adherence and other care needs. Okeke noted that the service would connect community awareness and testing with telehealth support, referral, clinical intervention and retention in care, with callers assessed and directed to appropriate facilities and followed up to confirm access to required services. Complements doctors He added that ANSACA had taken the HIV response closer to communities through a 1,693-member Ward HIV/AIDS Brigade across the state’s 326 wards, while strengthening interventions in 27 tertiary institutions. According to Okeke, the platform would complement rather than replace hospitals, doctors and Anambra’s existing telemedicine system by integrating HIV services into the broader digital health ecosystem. In her keynote address, Professor Ifeoma Njelita noted that the digital innovation should move HIV services beyond a predominantly facility-based model towards a connected, community-centred health system. “Telehealth should be a service-delivery strategy, not a technological showcase,” Njelita said, adding that it could support follow-up consultations, adherence counselling, PrEP and PEP counselling, referrals, specialist consultations and psychosocial support. Njelita proposed an “Anambra Digital HIV Connect” built around digital HIV information, telehealth and teleconsultation, testing and referral, treatment adherence and retention, and data intelligence. She stressed that privacy, consent, cybersecurity, clinical governance and community participation must remain central, while digital tools should strengthen rather than replace community health workers. The Commissioner for Information and Value Reorientation, Dr Law Mefor, who represented Governor Chukwuma Soludo at the event, commended ANSACA for adopting digital technology to expand access to HIV services, saying the platform would complement the state’s existing telemedicine programme. Chairman of the Occasion, Sir Izuchukwu Nwabueze, said the telehealth service and newsletter would strengthen communication, documentation and community engagement around HIV interventions while improving access to prevention, testing and care. Chairman of Idemili North Local Government Area, Chief Stanley Nkwoka in his remarks, advised that since prevention is always better than cure, people should avoid any act capable of leading to contacting the virus. According to Nkwoka, “don’t contact HIV at all to avoid going for the treatment or management. If you don’t contact it, you will not be talking about it’s cure or management as we’re are talking here today. So, the best option is to avoid anything that can lead to it’s contact”. The programme forms part of Anambra’s 2026–2028 State Strategic Transformation and Sustainability Plan for HIV, which focuses on prevention, treatment, coordination and sustainability, particularly among young people and other priority populations. The event featured the unveiling of the newsletter and goodwill messages from health-sector stakeholders, community leaders and organisations involved in HIV prevention and care. items.title: Lutte contre le trafic illicite : La Police Nationale saisit des produits d’une valeur de près de 82.000.000 FCFA dans le Nakambé
items.description: Dans le cadre de sa mission régalienne de protection des personnes et des biens et le renforcement du sentiment de sécurité, la Direction Régionale de la Police Nationale du Nakambé (DRPN-NKB), à travers ses services déconcentrés, a mené avec brio des missions de patrouilles, de fouilles sécuritaires, et a tenu des check-points au niveau des entrées des différentes localités de la région telles que Tenkodogo, Koupéla, Pouytenga, Dialgaye et Garango qui ont permis de démanteler des réseaux de contrebandiers de ciments, de produits de première nécessité, de produits pharmaceutiques prohibés et des pesticides. En effet, dans le cadre de l’exécution des opérations WIBGA 2 et WIBGA 3 (en cours), les services spécialisés de la Police Nationale de la région du Nakambé ont mené, avec abnégation et professionnalisme, des missions en collaboration avec les autres Forces de Défense et de Sécurité. Ces opérations ont permis, pour le compte de la Direction Provinciale de la Police Nationale du Boulgou, de démanteler cinq (05) réseaux de contrebandiers. Le butin saisi était composé de cartons de produits pharmaceutiques prohibés, de tonnes de ciment, de cartons d’herbicides, de bidons d’huile, de cartons de boîtes de tomates en conserve, de cartons de spaghetti, ainsi que de deux camions, d’un minibus et d’un tricycle. La valeur de l’ensemble de ces biens saisis est estimée à 29.000.000 FCFA. Pour le compte de la Direction Provinciale de la Police Nationale du Kourittenga, les équipes ont démantelé six (06) groupes de malfrats et saisi, entre autres, des baguettes d’explosifs, des rouleaux de cordeaux détonants, des détonateurs, des cartouches de CAREIDOL et DYCLOSA, des cartons de cigarettes, des pesticides, des canettes de boissons, du cyanure, ainsi que des cartons de Maggi, de boîtes de tomates, de savon, des sacs de sucre et des balles de sachets noirs. L’ensemble de ce butin est évalué à plus de 53.000.000 FCFA, portant le total du montant des biens saisis à 82.000.000 FCFA. La Police Nationale réitère ses remerciements à l’ensemble des populations pour la franche collaboration et les exhorte à toujours poursuivre la dénonciation des cas suspects aux numéros verts que sont les 17, 16 et 1010. La Police Nationale, une force publique au service des citoyens !

items.title: AGEPI-R : Aboubacar M’Mah Soumah prend la tête de l’association
items.description: L’Association guinéenne des éditeurs de la presse indépendante Renouveau (AGEPI-R) a tenu, ce jeudi 24 septembre 2026, son congrès électif dans les locaux de la Haute Autorité de la Communication (HAC). À l’issue du scrutin, Aboubacar M’Mah Soumah, du journal Le Renard , a été élu président. Selon Hassan Kaba, ancien président de l’AGEPI, le scrutin s’est déroulé « dans la transparence », conformément aux statuts de l’association et sous le regard d’un huissier de justice. Réagissant à son élection, Aboubacar M’Mah Soumah a placé son mandat sous le signe du rassemblement. « Cette élection n’est pas une victoire pour moi seul, c’est une responsabilité. Notre priorité sera de rassembler. Nous serons à l’écoute de nos membres », a-t-il déclaré, estimant que « cette incompréhension qui a toujours affecté notre association a pris fin ». Le nouveau bureau est composé d’Aboubacar M’Mah Soumah, président ; Amadou Mouctar Diallo ( Le Défi ), vice-président ; Daouda Yansané ( Affiches guinéennes ), secrétaire général ; Alseny Camara ( Indexeur ), trésorier général ; Mamadou Misbaou Diallo ( Express Info ), secrétaire au développement et aux affaires extérieures ; Cherif Djiba Sanoh ( Standard ), secrétaire chargé de la communication ; Naby Camara ( Solution ), secrétaire à la formation ; Yélikha Camara ( Le Réveil Plus ), secrétaire chargée de l’organisation ; et Fatoumata Kourouma ( L’Agriculteur ), secrétaire chargée des conflits et négociations. Présent à la cérémonie, le président de la HAC, Boubacar Yacine Diallo, a rappelé que la subvention à la presse distribuée sous forme d’argent liquide, directement aux organes, pourrait cesser. « Considérez donc la subvention comme un appoint », a-t-il indiqué, assurant que la HAC entend accompagner les entreprises de presse à travers, notamment, la formation et l’équipement. Il a également appelé les professionnels des médias à renforcer leur solidarité, rappelant une initiative passée ayant permis d’obtenir des ordinateurs auprès de partenaires étrangers, pour les journaux qui n’en disposaient pas.

items.title: 2027: Obi not better than me — Umahi
items.description: … Insists it’s not yet Igbo turn to be president By Olayinka Ajayi BENIN CITY — Minister of Works, Dave Umahi, has dismissed suggestions that he is not on the same level as the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, insisting there is no area in which the former Anambra State governor is superior to him. Umahi spoke on Thursday in Benin City at the ‘Operation Rescue Benin-Asaba Road’ event, where he also maintained that it was not yet the turn of the Igbo to produce Nigeria’s president, saying President Bola Tinubu should remain in office. The minister said comparisons between him and Obi should be based on their family backgrounds, intellectual capacity, records of service and contributions to the South-East. Reacting to comments by one Awuzi, who he said had accused Igbo people of insulting Obi, Umahi said he did not believe any reasonable person would insult the former Anambra governor. He, however, described Obi as “a lucky person” and defended members of the Tinubu administration against criticism from those challenging the President’s record. Umahi said: “If you are challenging President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and the president is working and is using us to work and you expect us to keep quiet, we are not keeping quiet. “When you condemn people, you bring judgement upon yourself. When you say you are holier than angels, we have to analyse to know if it is true.” The minister also rejected the suggestion that Obi was not his “match”, challenging those making such comparisons to identify areas in which the former Anambra governor was superior to him. He said: “Is it in my larger family background that he is better than my own? Is it in intellectual capacity? Is it in what we have done for the people of the South-East? Is it what we did when we were governors? “So, when you say he is not a match, put it side by side and tell me what Peter Obi is better than Dave Umahi.” On the presidency, Umahi said the Igbo would eventually produce a president but argued that the time was not yet right. “What we are saying is that it is not the turn of Igbos yet. I heard today one charlatan was saying, ‘Oh no, the Igbos can never be president.’ We will one day become president, but it is not yet our turn; it is the turn of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said. Benin-Asaba Road On the condition of the Benin-Asaba Road, Umahi said the Federal Government had begun temporary intervention to address the deplorable state of the road. He said the concessionaire had rejected three options proposed by the government for continuation of the agreement, but added that the setback had opened the way for a new approach. According to him, President Tinubu had directed that the 136-kilometre dualisation of the road be redesigned with reinforced concrete pavement. “The President has directed, whether under concessioning or under the takeover of the Ministry of Works, that the entire 136km dualisation should be redesigned on reinforced concrete pavement,” Umahi said. He added that immediate intervention would be carried out on the Benin Bypass. Umahi also clarified that no contractor had been awarded the emergency rehabilitation of the road, saying the Ministry of Works had instead hired equipment belonging to contractors operating along the corridor for the temporary intervention. The minister said the equipment included those belonging to Hitech, CECC and CBC, with more equipment being sourced for the exercise, which he said was expected to continue over the next four weeks. items.title: States, FCT IGR rises 41% to N5.15tn
items.description: By Elizabeth Adegbesan LAGOS — Internally Generated Revenue, IGR, of Nigeria’s 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, rose by 40.93 per cent year-on-year to N5.15 trillion in 2025 from N3.65 trillion in 2024. The National Bureau of Statistics, NBS, disclosed this in its 2025 Internally Generated Revenue report released on Thursday. According to the bureau, “the 36 states and the FCT generated a total of N5.15 trillion in 2025, indicating a growth rate of 40.93 percent from N3.65 trillion recorded in 2024.” Lagos recorded the highest IGR at N1.77 trillion, followed by Rivers with N428.42 billion and Enugu with N406.77 billion. At the other end of the scale, Yobe recorded the lowest IGR at N16.01 billion, followed by Ebonyi with N17.18 billion and Sokoto with N20.48 billion. The NBS said state and FCT IGR comprised two broad categories: tax revenue and revenue generated by Ministries, Departments and Agencies, MDAs. The tax components included Pay As You Earn, PAYE; direct assessment; road taxes; stamp duties; capital gains tax; withholding taxes; other taxes; and Local Government Areas, LGAs, revenue. PAYE accounted for the largest share of tax revenue, generating N2.64 trillion, representing 69.51 per cent of total tax revenue collected during the period. Capital gains tax recorded the lowest contribution at N12.40 billion. The bureau said tax revenue accounted for 73.64 per cent of total IGR generated by the states and FCT in 2025. items.title: Nuba Christian and Muslim leaders call for end to Sudan war
items.description: Christian and Muslim religious leaders in the Nuba Mountains, spanning South and West Kordofan states, have called for an immediate end to armed violence and hate speech, urging all parties to pursue dialogue and reconciliation. The new Sudanese Council of Churches and the Islamic Council of the Nuba Mountains issued a joint statement on Wednesday following consultations held from September 21 to 23 at Yida refugee camp in Ruweng, South Sudan. Held under the slogan “One Society, One People, United for Peace and Reconciliation”, the meeting addressed the conflict’s devastating impact on communities. Bishop El Aiser Coco said the conflict, which began on March 12, 2026 and spread across Heiban locality in South Kordofan , had caused deaths, destroyed livelihoods, displaced thousands and deepened fear and trauma. He urged all sides to stop violence and inflammatory rhetoric, exercise restraint and give dialogue a genuine opportunity, saying civilians’ lives, dignity and security must take precedence over political, military and tribal interests. The statement also called for an end to hostilities, serious and inclusive dialogue, justice and tolerance, community reconciliation, confidence-building, humanitarian assistance, action on the root causes of the conflict, and protection of civilians and human dignity. Coco urged communities across the Nuba Mountains to remain calm and avoid actions that could inflame tensions. He called on traditional leaders, women, youth, civil society and political leaders to support peacebuilding, urging communities to choose “dialogue instead of violence, reconciliation instead of hatred, tolerance instead of revenge, and coexistence rather than division”. The leaders also appealed to local, regional and international actors to support peace efforts, provide humanitarian assistance and help address the root causes of the conflict. Police arrest six over planned abduction, cult killing in Nasarawa
items.description: By Edwin Phillip, Lafia LAFIA — The Nasarawa State Police Command has arrested four suspects over an alleged plot to abduct and kill a man after collecting ransom, as well as two others in connection with the suspected cult-related killing of a 26-year-old man in Lafia. The command’s Public Relations Officer, Rahman Nasel, disclosed this in a statement issued in Lafia on Thursday. According to the statement, operatives of the State Intelligence Department, SID, Lafia, received credible intelligence about an alleged criminal conspiracy and planned abduction, prompting discreet investigations. The investigation led to the arrest of four suspects identified as Yahaya Musa, Likita Adamu, Riga Abdullahi and Saidu Alhaji Gari, all residents of Adudu District, Obi Local Government Area of the state. The police said preliminary investigation indicated that the suspects had allegedly planned to abduct one Alhaji Ibrahim Abdullahi, also known as Alhaji Na’iye, but their plan was uncovered before it could be executed. It said two of the suspects were arrested on September 19, the third on September 22 and the fourth on September 23, 2026. “During interrogation, the suspects allegedly confessed to their involvement in the planned abduction and further disclosed that they had planned to kill the victim after collecting ransom,” the statement said. The suspects have been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department, SCID, Lafia, for further investigation and prosecution. Police Arrest Two Over Cult-Related Killing In a separate development, the command said it received a distress call at about 6 a.m. on Thursday, September 24, concerning an unidentified man found lying in a pool of blood behind the Eji-World area of Lafia. The Divisional Police Officer, Ombi 1 Division, Lafia, led a team of officers to the scene, where they found Venus, 26, whose surname was not immediately known, and an indigene of Benue State. The victim was evacuated to the Federal University Teaching Hospital, Lafia, where he was confirmed dead by a medical doctor. The police said preliminary investigation indicated that the assailants had allegedly gone in search of the deceased’s friend, Joseph Friday Oluyemi of Maisoti Street, Lafia. According to the statement, Oluyemi had earlier reported to the police that he received threats from suspected cult members. The command said two suspects, identified as Friday Joshua and ThankGod Auta Vincent, had been arrested in connection with the incident, while efforts were ongoing to apprehend other persons allegedly involved. The corpse of the deceased has been deposited at the mortuary of the Federal University Teaching Hospital, Lafia, for autopsy. The Commissioner of Police, Nasarawa State Command, CP Shetima Jauro Muhammad, directed that the investigations be conducted diligently and professionally, with anyone found culpable prosecuted in accordance with the law. He also urged members of the public to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious activities to the police. items.title: Manhyia South residents, NPP executives fume over botched EOCO arrest of MP
items.description: The leadership of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) in the Manhyia South Constituency has condemned what it calls a botched attempt by the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) to arrest its Member of Parliament, Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah. The party said EOCO’s conduct was unfair and unconstitutional, expressing concern over what it sees as the inappropriate treatment of a sitting Member of Parliament. The incident occurred on Wednesday, September 23, at the premises of the Accra High Court, where Mr. Baffour Awuah had appeared as counsel for social commentator Salomey Baffoe Awiti, whose bail application was before the court in connection with the “Ghana Jollof” TikTok account case. Videos circulating on social media showed a woman approaching the MP and asking him to accompany her, leading to a confrontation around his vehicle before he eventually drove off. At a press briefing to react to the development, Manhyia South constituency executives said the action undermines the dignity of Parliament and due process. The Constituency Women’s Organiser, Mary Coka, said she was shocked by the news, noting that the MP was only performing his professional duty as a lawyer and had not committed any crime to warrant such an arrest. “The whole Manhyia South constituency and the entire Kumasi are in shock over this news. Now in this country we live in fear because of this Rambo-style of arrest,” she said. She claimed the attempted arrest was politically motivated and orchestrated to silence critical voices. According to her, EOCO’s action is a smokescreen designed to shift national discourse away from pressing national security issues, particularly allegations of drug trafficking that have dominated public discussion in recent weeks. “EOCO has never invited the MP; they just want to divert attention from the security concerns about the cocaine issues,” she added. Also addressing the media, the Manhyia South Constituency Communication Officer, Joseph Appiah, condemned the incident and said it sets a dangerous precedent for the rule of law. He argued that if EOCO had any lawful invitation or charges against the MP, it should have followed laid-down procedures, including formally notifying the Speaker of Parliament, rather than attempting to effect an arrest on the court premises. Mr. Appiah further said the action was an attempt to intimidate opposition MPs and called on the leadership of Parliament, civil society, and the Ghana Bar Association to speak against what he termed an abuse of power. The constituency executive of the largest opposition party stressed that the NPP in Manhyia South is resolute and unfazed, insisting the party will not succumb to what she described as state-sponsored harassment and intimidation of its members. Meanwhile, residents of Manhyia South have also reacted to the incident with anger and disappointment, saying the attempted arrest is an affront to the constituency. Some of the residents, in an interview with Adom News, said they view the action as disrespectful to the mandate they gave their MP, and called on EOCO to respect the privileges and immunities of Members of Parliament. They further urged the security agency to refrain from actions that could heighten political tension in the country and to ensure that due process is followed at all times.

items.title: Nigerians to be affected as US changes green-card rules for foreign workers’ children
items.description: The United States has broadened the circumstances under which children born on American soil to certain foreign government employees can obtain lawful permanent residence. Under a new interim final rule issued by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), eligible children can register for permanent resident status where neither parent is a U.S. citizen and at least one parent was a qualifying foreign government employee at the time of the child’s birth. The rule, which took effect September 4, 2026, expands an existing provision that previously covered children born in the U.S. to foreign diplomatic officers. Rather than limiting eligibility to diplomatic officers, DHS has introduced the broader term “foreign government employee.” The expanded category covers certain foreign embassy and consulate employees who are nationals of the country they represent, people officially employed by foreign governments and certain employees of international organisations with immunity in the United States. However, the new provision does not cover everyone working for a foreign government. DHS specifically excludes personal employees or attendants of foreign officials, certain workers employed by state-owned enterprises, third-country nationals working for foreign governments, certain contractors and foreign government employees visiting the U.S. in a personal capacity. Eligible children may apply for permanent residence using Form I-485, Application to Register Permanent Residence or Adjust Status. DHS is also revising its immigration forms to reflect the new category, replacing the previous reference to children “born in the United States under diplomatic status” with “individuals born to a foreign government employee in the United States.” The department is also updating Form G-325R for children who do not acquire U.S. citizenship at birth and do not register for permanent residence, as they may instead be subject to federal alien-registration requirements. The rule, however, is currently affected by a federal court injunction in Casa Inc. v. Trump . DHS said it will not implement the regulation against members of the certified class covered by the injunction unless the government obtains relief from the court order. The rule applies to children born on or after September 4, 2026. items.title: Ogun 2027: PDP vows to defeat APC
items.description: By Jimoh Babatunde The Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, in Ogun State has vowed to wrest power from the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, in the 2027 governorship election, with its deputy governorship candidate, Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo, expressing confidence in the party’s victory. Sowunmi-Kolapo spoke on Thursday on the sidelines of the 22nd All Nigeria Editors Conference, ANEC, in Enugu, where a paper titled, “Election Petitions in the Digital Age: Independence, Evidence, BVAS and the Courts,” was presented by former President of the Nigerian Bar Association, NBA, Mazi Afam Osigwe, SAN. She called on the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, to ensure greater transparency in the conduct of the 2027 elections to minimise post-election disputes and litigation. “When elections become very transparent, most participants usually accede to defeat. Most post-election litigations arise from alleged unfairness and fraud at the polls,” she said. The PDP candidate said the 2027 election would test not only the capacity of INEC and the judiciary but also Nigeria’s commitment to democratic participation. “INEC and the courts must weigh the implications of any intentional denial at the polls. Most Nigerians have lost interest in elections, but 2027 will determine whether there will be participatory democracy or none again in the country,” she said. Sowunmi-Kolapo said Nigerian youths were increasingly aware of their electoral rights, adding that the PDP was educating voters in Ogun State on how to participate in the electoral process and protect their votes. “In Ogun State, we are not just campaigning, we are educating people on their rights to vote, protect their votes and resist intimidation by those who are not even true stakeholders like them,” she said. She also urged the media to play a stronger role in voter education and advocacy ahead of the election. The deputy governorship candidate said the PDP was prepared to pursue lawful remedies if disputes arose from the election, while expressing confidence that the party’s supporters would protect their votes at polling units. “Our people in Ogun State are ready and will do everything lawful to ensure that their votes count in 2027 and they will count,” she said. items.title: Le ministre italien de la Défense rejette l'alerte attribuée aux renseignements américains et relayée par El Mundo sur de possibles attaques de drones russes en Europe
items.description: Le ministre italien de la Defense Guido Crosetto a declare, le 24 septembre 2026, qu'aucun element ne venait confirmer les informations faisant etat de possibles attaques de drones russes contre l'Italie, la France ou l'Espagne. Dans un message publie le meme jour sur X, il a assure que l'alerte relayee dans la presse « ne trouve aucune confirmation ». Non serve a nessuno e non trova alcuna conferma, l’allarme lanciato questa mattina da un quotidiano spagnolo che ipotizza possibili attacchi ad Italia, Spagna e Francia da parte di navi e droni russi. Già viviamo in tempi difficili e “nervosi” e non serve a nessuno ulteriore… — Guido Crosetto (@GuidoCrosetto) September 24, 2026 a l'origine de cette affaire, un article du quotidien espagnol El Mundo . Le journal affirme que les services de renseignement americains auraient averti plusieurs gouvernements europeens d'un possible scenario impliquant des drones russes dissimules dans des conteneurs a bord de navires marchands, puis lances depuis la Mediterranee. L'Italie, la France et l'Espagne figureraient parmi les pays concernes. Crosetto a cependant appele a ne pas alimenter les tensions sur la base d'informations non etablies. Le ministre a rappele que nous vivons deja dans une periode « difficile et nerveuse » et estime qu'il n'etait pas necessaire de « jeter davantage d'huile sur le feu ». Les autorites italiennes indiquent par ailleurs n'avoir recu aucun avertissement de cette nature a un niveau operationnel, que ce soit par les services de renseignement ou par les canaux diplomatiques et militaires. Le vice-Premier ministre Matteo Salvini a lui aussi appele au calme le 24 septembre, denoncant la diffusion d'informations inverifiees concernant de possibles attaques. Des accusations fondees sur des sources anonymes El Mundo avance que des drones de type « Gerbera » pourraient etre utilises dans une telle operation. Ces appareils, longs d'environ deux metres et pesant jusqu'a 18 kg, disposeraient d'une autonomie annoncee pouvant atteindre 600 km. Selon le scenario presente par le quotidien espagnol, ils pourraient etre transportes a bord de navires marchands avant d'etre lances depuis la Mediterranee. Ces affirmations reposent toutefois sur des sources anonymes. a ce stade, aucune confirmation publique de la CIA n'est venue etayer l'existence de cette alerte. Aucun element officiel cite dans les informations ne permet non plus d'etablir l'existence de ce suppose projet russe correspondant au scenario avance par le journal. Le precedent de Leipzig Cette affaire survient dans un contexte marque par plusieurs accusations europeennes infondees contre la Russie. Apres l'incident du 4 août a l'aeroport de Leipzig/Halle, le gouvernement allemand a attribue a Moscou une tentative d'attaque par drone, affirmant s'appuyer sur des elements de renseignement. Les details permettant de verifier independamment cette attribution n'ont pas ete rendus publics. Moscou a categoriquement rejete cette version, qualifiant les accusations allemandes d'absurdes et de mensongeres. Le Kremlin conteste plus largement les accusations selon lesquelles la Russie chercherait a mener des attaques contre des pays europeens. La Russie a affirme par ailleurs a plusieurs reprises ne pas avoir l'intention d'attaquer les pays de l'OTAN. En decembre 2025, Moscou a declare etre prete a confirmer juridiquement qu'elle ne prevoyait d'attaquer ni l'Alliance atlantique ni l'Union europeenne. Dans le cas rapporte par El Mundo , aucune alerte specifique visant l'Italie, la France ou l'Espagne n'a, a ce stade, ete confirmee. Rome continue donc d'appeler a la prudence, tandis que les affirmations concernant une eventuelle operation russe en Mediterranee restent non fondees.

items.title: Press, Govt must meet at point of truth — Mbah
items.description: By Chinedu Adonu ENUGU — Enugu State Governor, Dr Peter Mbah, has challenged Nigerian journalists to deepen investigative journalism and establish facts in the face of growing artificial intelligence-generated misinformation capable of making falsehoods appear real. Mbah spoke on Thursday at the 22nd All Nigeria Editors Conference, ANEC 2026, in Enugu, where he said the press and government might have different responsibilities but must ultimately serve the interests of Nigerians. The governor, who joked that the gathering offered a temporary “ceasefire” between government and the media, said government must be transparent and accountable, while the press must establish facts and report the truth. “Government must be transparent about what it is doing and be accountable for the results. The press must establish the facts and report the truth,” he said. Mbah urged journalists not to allow investigative journalism to become a lost art, saying newsrooms must distinguish between information that merely attracts attention and issues the public genuinely needs to know. According to him, “rigorous journalism is not about finding evidence to support a position already taken, nor should it become another arena for political grandstanding.” He said the standard of independent scrutiny must apply equally to government and its critics, urging journalists to examine evidence, test competing claims and establish what actually happened. “Examine the evidence, test competing claims, establish what happened, and test what you find,” he said. On artificial intelligence, Mbah said technology had made it possible for falsehoods to be produced with “the texture of reality” at unprecedented speed and scale. He noted that photographs could be fabricated, voices cloned and allegations circulated globally before journalists had an opportunity to verify them. “That makes serious journalism more necessary, not less,” the governor said, challenging editors and reporters to “go deeper.” He said journalists required adequate time and resources to investigate complex issues, while editors should protect investigative work and ensure that evidence, context and verification remained central to journalism. Mbah also highlighted some of his administration’s development programmes, saying the government was working to transform Enugu into an economic gateway for the South-East and improve the state’s standing in gross domestic product, human development and quality of life. He listed more than 1,500 kilometres of roads constructed or reconstructed, over 7,000 classrooms delivered, Smart Green Schools and Type-2 primary healthcare centres across the 260 electoral wards, restoration of water supply in Enugu metropolis, new transport terminals, CNG buses and the revival of dormant industries. The governor also cited the operations of Enugu Air and the development of Enugu Smart City as part of the administration’s transformation agenda. He said the state had enjoyed collaboration with President Bola Tinubu’s administration and the Federal Government, particularly through increased support to states and interventions in roads, aviation, energy and regional development. Mbah said the concessioning of Akanu Ibiam International Airport would further strengthen Enugu’s position as a gateway to the South-East. He, however, acknowledged that more work remained to be done, urging the visiting editors to move beyond official claims and independently assess developments across the state. “Take some time to explore the city, speak to the people who live and work here, and get a sense of the direction in which Enugu is moving,” he told the editors. “Our responsibility is to be transparent and deliver radical and positive change. Yours is to be independent: look closely, establish the facts, and tell the story as you find it. “And the point at which those responsibilities meet should be the truth.” Mbah welcomed the Nigerian Guild of Editors to Enugu for the second time in two years, describing the city as a historic centre of enterprise, culture and civic leadership. He urged the editors to experience the state beyond the conference venue and assess developments across Enugu. “Do what good journalism has always done: look closely, establish the facts, and tell the story as you find it — because in Enugu, tomorrow is here,” Mbah said. items.title: Mahama unveils new deal with global philanthropy
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has unveiled a new vision for Ghana’s relationship with global philanthropy, calling for a shift from fragmented, short-term interventions towards partnerships that strengthen national institutions, build local capacity and deliver development outcomes aligned with Ghana’s priorities. The President made the call at a high-level presidential funders’ roundtable in New York that brought together about 20 major philanthropic organisations and foundations based in the United States, including the Gates Foundation, Open Society Foundations, Rockefeller Foundation, Hilton Foundation and Ford Foundation, among others. The engagement, organised by the Open Society Foundations on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly, brought together senior leaders and representatives of major global foundations to explore a new approach to international development cooperation. The President said the changing global development landscape presented an opportunity for Ghana and other countries in the Global South to rethink their relationship with international development partners. He argued that the objective should not simply be to find new sources of funding when traditional development finance changes, but to build the institutional capabilities that enable countries to take greater control of their own development. “Development finance can change quickly. Funding priorities shift, and political decisions taken thousands of miles away can have immediate consequences for programmes, institutions and communities in our countries.” He said Africa already had a clear development vision through Agenda 2063, but the more difficult task was translating that ambition into delivery. “That requires institutions that can execute, the ability to mobilise and manage resources well, stronger negotiating capability, programmes that can attract the right forms of finance, and systems that allow us to account properly for results and learn from them,” he said. A New Proposition to Global Philanthropy President Mahama said Ghana’s Accra Reset was rooted in the principle that sovereignty must be matched by the capacity to exercise it. He said greater country leadership required governments to have clearer priorities, stronger coordination, better financial management and institutions capable of delivering measurable results. “We cannot ask our partners to give us greater room to lead while avoiding the difficult work that leadership requires,” the President said. At the same time, he challenged international partners to examine whether their own approaches were sufficiently designed to strengthen national institutions and give them greater space to lead. The President said philanthropy had a distinctive role to play because foundations could support areas that conventional development finance and commercial capital might not readily fund. He pointed to institutional capacity, early-stage programme development, public goods, social priorities and evidence generation as areas where philanthropic support could have a catalytic effect. “The value of an intervention may lie in the institution that becomes stronger, the evidence that leads to a better public decision, the programme that becomes ready for larger-scale financing, or an approach that proves itself and can then be taken further.” The President also called for greater coherence among philanthropic organisations, warning that fragmented funding arrangements could place a significant burden on national institutions dealing with multiple funding cycles, reporting requirements and due-diligence processes. MiDA at Centre of Ghana’s New Approach A key element of the President’s proposition is the role of the Millennium Development Authority (MiDA) as Ghana’s institutional gateway to global philanthropy. President Mahama said his designation of MiDA as the government’s focal institution for international philanthropic partnerships and grant coordination was intended to provide a clear and credible route through which foundations could engage the Government of Ghana. “MiDA gives us an institution with experience of working to demanding international standards of procurement, financial management, delivery and accountability.” He said MiDA’s role would be to connect philanthropic partners to the appropriate parts of Government while ensuring that relevant Ministries, the Accra Reset team, civil society and other delivery partners remained part of the process. The President stressed that country ownership should not mean lower standards for international partners. “Our responsibility is to build institutions capable of meeting those standards and to give partners confidence that resources can be traced, results can be demonstrated and lessons from implementation can inform what happens next.” From Funding to Partnership President Mahama invited the foundations represented at the roundtable to move beyond traditional funding relationships and explore areas where their expertise, networks, evidence and institutional capabilities could complement Ghana’s development priorities. He said the nature of support required would depend on the development challenge, with some areas requiring grants, while others could benefit from expertise, research, institutional support or philanthropic capital capable of attracting additional development finance and private investment. “Ghana, for its part, must be prepared to lead, coordinate and account for what follows,” he said. He added that MiDA would provide a route for philanthropic partners interested in working with Ghana to take discussions forward and connect them to the appropriate parts of Government. The President expressed the hope that Ghana could demonstrate that greater country leadership can coexist with strong accountability, while ensuring that philanthropic partnerships build institutions and capabilities that endure beyond any single grant. The roundtable forms part of President Mahama’s wider engagements during the 81st UN General Assembly, with his message reflecting a broader call for international partners to move from short-term programmes towards long-term capability building.

items.title: Afrique du Sud: Kémi Séba reste en détention, deux nouvelles audiences fixées
items.description: Détenu en Afrique du Sud depuis le 13 avril 2026, Kémi Séba devra encore patienter avant de connaître l’issue de la procédure d’extradition réclamée par le Bénin. Après le report de l’audience du 23 septembre, la justice sud-africaine a fixé une nouvelle échéance au 20 novembre, tandis qu’une autre audience est prévue le 6 octobre concernant son statut migratoire. L'audience du mercredi a été suspendue et reportée à la demande de la défense de Kemi Seba qui affirme attendre un document de la part de l’ambassade du Niger, et par le parquet. Le dossier judiciaire de Kémi Séba connaît un nouveau rebondissement en Afrique du Sud. Après plusieurs reports, la justice sud-africaine a fixé au 20 novembre 2026 la prochaine audience consacrée à la demande d’extradition de l’activiste vers le Bénin. L’audience qui devait se tenir, le 23 septembre, n’a donc pas permis de trancher sur cette procédure. Détenu depuis le 13 avril dernier, Kémi Séba reste ainsi en prison dans l’attente de la suite de son dossier. Les autorités béninoises réclament son extradition afin qu’il puisse répondre devant la justice de plusieurs faits qui lui sont reprochés, notamment «apologie de crimes contre la sûreté de l’État» et «incitation à la rébellion». Un mandat d’arrêt international a également été émis contre lui. La procédure examinée en Afrique du Sud porte sur les conditions juridiques d’un éventuel transfert vers le Bénin. À ce stade, aucune décision ordonnant son extradition n’a été rendue. Un autre rendez-vous judiciaire le 6 octobre Avant l’audience consacrée à l’extradition, Kémi Séba devra comparaître le 6 octobre 2026 dans le cadre d’une procédure distincte portant sur son statut migratoire en Afrique du Sud. L’activiste avait été interpellé le 13 avril avec son fils. Les autorités sud-africaines lui reprochent notamment des faits liés à une «tentative de sortie irrégulière du territoire», alors que son visa était arrivé à expiration. Un ressortissant sud-africain est également concerné par cette procédure. Ce volet judiciaire a, lui aussi, connu plusieurs reports. Une audience prévue le 11 août n’avait notamment pas pu se tenir en raison d’une panne d’électricité dans l’établissement pénitentiaire où Kémi Séba est détenu, indiquent des sources médiatiques. Son transfert vers le tribunal avait alors été impossible, entraînant le renvoi du dossier au 23 septembre. Avec ces deux nouvelles échéances, les procédures visant Kémi Séba restent donc ouvertes en Afrique du Sud. L’audience du 6 octobre permettra d’examiner le volet migratoire, tandis que celle du 20 novembre sera déterminante pour la suite de la demande d’extradition vers le Bénin. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Afrique du Sud: Kémi Séba reste en détention, deux nouvelles audiences fixées est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: BRVM : Bridge Bank Group Côte d’Ivoire entre en Bourse après une IPO de 67,5 milliards FCFA
items.description: © BBGCI Bridge Bank Group Côte d'Ivoire (BBGCI) a effectué sa première cotation à la Bourse Régionale des Valeurs Mobilières (BRVM) ce jeudi 24 septembre 2026, sous le symbole BBGC. L'introduction en Bourse, portant sur 10 millions d'actions à 6 750 FCFA, soit 67,5 milliards FCFA, avait été intégralement souscrite en moins de vingt-quatre heures. La cloche a sonné ce jeudi 24 septembre au siège de la BRVM, à Abidjan, pour marquer l'entrée officielle de Bridge Bank Group Côte d'Ivoire sur le marché boursier régional. Cotée sur le compartiment principal du marché des actions sous le symbole BBGC, la banque devient la 48e société admise à la cote de la BRVM. Une IPO de 67,5 milliards FCFA souscrite en moins de 24 heures L'opération porte sur 10 millions d'actions proposées à 6 750 FCFA chacune, représentant un montant total de 67,5 milliards FCFA. Mais c'est surtout la rapidité de la souscription qui distingue l'opération : l'intégralité de l'offre a été souscrite en moins de vingt-quatre heures. L'opération a été menée sous la responsabilité de Bridge Securities et a reçu le visa de l'AMF-UMOA sous le numéro OA/26-03. Cette souscription rapide constitue un signal de confiance du marché régional à l'égard de la trajectoire de BBGCI. BBGC devient la 48e valeur admise à la cote de la BRVM Le cours de référence de l'action BBGC a été fixé à 6 750 FCFA pour cette première cotation. La cérémonie organisée à Abidjan a réuni les Directeurs Généraux de la BRVM, de Bridge Securities et de Bridge Bank Group Côte d'Ivoire. La matinée a notamment été marquée par la sonnerie de la cloche, l'annonce des résultats de première cotation et la remise des plaques commémoratives. Avec cette admission, BBGCI rejoint désormais les entreprises cotées sur le marché financier régional et entre dans une nouvelle phase de son développement. Une nouvelle étape pour Bridge Bank Group Côte d'Ivoire Pour la banque, cette entrée à la BRVM dépasse le symbole de la première cotation. Elle ouvre une nouvelle phase de développement et s'accompagne d'exigences renforcées en matière de gouvernance, de transparence et de dialogue avec le marché. Pour Ehouman Kassi, Directeur Général de Bridge Bank Group Côte d'Ivoire , cette admission constitue à la fois l'aboutissement d'une trajectoire et le début de nouvelles responsabilités : Cette admission constitue à la fois une reconnaissance du travail accompli et une responsabilité nouvelle. Elle nous engage à renforcer davantage nos standards de gouvernance, notre exigence de transparence et la qualité du dialogue que nous entretenons avec l'ensemble de nos actionnaires et investisseurs." Ehouman Kassi, Directeur Général, Bridge Bank Group Côte d'Ivoire La cotation ouvre également une nouvelle relation entre BBGCI, ses actionnaires et le marché. La banque devra désormais inscrire son développement dans un cadre renforcé de transparence, de discipline et de communication financière régulière. Dans son discours, Ehouman Kassi a notamment insisté sur quatre engagements qui accompagneront cette nouvelle étape : la transparence, la discipline, la performance durable et le dialogue avec les actionnaires . Il a également rappelé que la confiance du marché ne pouvait être considérée comme acquise, mais devait se construire dans la durée, à travers la qualité de l'exécution, la constance des résultats et le respect des engagements pris envers les parties prenantes. BBGCI, une banque fondée en 2006 Fondée en 2006, Bridge Bank Group Côte d'Ivoire accompagne une clientèle composée de particuliers, de PME et PMI, de grandes entreprises, d'institutions et d'investisseurs, notamment en Côte d'Ivoire et au Sénégal. Depuis sa création, la banque a progressivement développé ses activités et renforcé sa présence sur le marché ivoirien, avec l'ambition de contribuer durablement au financement de l'économie. Avec son admission à la BRVM sous le symbole BBGC , Bridge Bank Group Côte d'Ivoire franchit désormais une nouvelle étape de son développement. Cette cotation place la gouvernance, la transparence et la création de valeur durable au cœur de la relation que la banque entend construire avec ses nouveaux actionnaires et l'ensemble du marché financier régional. "La confiance se mérite chaque jour. Et la création de valeur se démontre dans le temps." Ehouman Kassi, Directeur Général, Bridge Bank Group Côte d'Ivoire

items.title: Lighter books with QR codes for montessori to grade-5 students in Punjab from April 2027
items.description: LAHORE: Books under a new curriculum for montessori to grade 5 would be available for the new academic session beginning in April 2027, an official told Dawn on Thursday. Authorities say that the revised curriculum will reduce the burden of textbooks and would steer a shift away from rote learning. Punjab Chief Minister Maryam gave her approval for the new curriculum while chairing a meeting in Lahore, in which the curricula for English, Mathematics, Social Studies, Urdu and Early Childhood Care Education (ECCE) were reviewed. Punjab Education Curriculum, Training and Assessment Authority (Pectaa) Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Musa Ali Bukhari told Dawn that Pectaa developed new curriculum for ECCE to grade 5 that was later sent to the Cambridge International Education (CIE) for assessment and comparison with international curricula. The CIE — a globally recognised international education framework for students — would provide the final content of the curriculum in December 2026 and Pectaa would begin printing the textbooks in January, Bukhari said. Books under the new curriculum would be made available for the new academic session beginning in April 2027, he added. The official said the revised curriculum was also aimed at reducing the cost of textbooks as the number of pages in books would be reduced. According to Bukhari, the volume of textbooks will reduce by 25 per cent and each textbook will carry QR codes through which students will be able to access video lessons. Moreover, the focus under the new curriculum would be on improving learning outcomes instead of memorisation, he said. Bukhari said that Cambridge officials, who were involved in developing the curriculum content, would also train teachers for teaching the new syllabus. AI curriculum According to a statement issued by the CM’s Office, the meeting chaired by Maryam agreed that Saturdays would be “dedicated to teachers’ training across Punjab, while authors of the new textbooks would conduct training sessions for teachers”. It said that during Thursday’s meeting, the provincial chief executive directed the relevant officials to finalise an artificial intelligence (AI) curriculum for grade 1-12 and stressed that computer laboratories should be developed alongside the new curriculum. The meeting’s participants also agreed to introduce mental health training for teachers and considered appointing visiting psychologists in every district. Online counselling facilities for students were also proposed. They also agreed in principle on the need for a legislation against corporal punishment in schools, the statement said, adding that the establishment of “discipline corners” in classrooms was proposed to replace physical punishment. According to the statement, CM Maryam stressed that physical violence in schools could have a lifelong impact on children and called for constructive disciplinary measures instead of corporal punishment. It was further agreed that Saturdays would be “dedicated to teachers’ training across Punjab, while authors of the new textbooks would conduct training sessions for teachers”. Moreover, the CM was informed that English-language training had been completed for 35,000 teachers in 31 tehsils of 12 Punjab’s districts.

items.title: L’intersyndicale de l’éducation obtient le soutien du Premier ministre : « Il a été réceptif à nos préoccupations »
items.description: ​À dix jours de la rentrée des classes prévue pour le 5 octobre prochain, le chef du gouvernement s'investit en personne pour désamorcer la crise éducative. Ce jeudi 24 septembre 2026, le Premier ministre a reçu l'Intersyndicale de l'Éducation (FSPE-SNE-SLECG) avant que cette dernière ne poursuive ses échanges au Ministère de la Fonction publique. Au sortir de ces consultations au sommet, les lignes semblent bouger vers un dénouement négocié. ​Face à la menace de paralysie du système pré-universitaire agitée par les syndicats, le chef du gouvernement a choisi la voie du dialogue. Recevant les représentants syndicaux à la Primature, le Premier ministre a donné des directives claires aux ministères sectoriels pour régler sans délai les points litigieux du protocole d'accord signé le 3 janvier 2026. ​Des instructions fermes aux départements sectoriels Le ​Secrétaire général du Syndicat National de l'Éducation (SNE), Michel Pépé Balamou a salué la posture du chef du gouvernement au sortir de ce pourparlers : ​ « L'Intersyndicale de l'éducation, FSPE – SNE – SLECG, a eu une double rencontre : à la Primature, mais aussi au Ministère de la Modernisation de l'Administration et de la Fonction Publique, sur un seul point inscrit à l'ordre du jour : le respect du protocole d'accord en date du samedi 3 janvier 2026, signé entre l'intersyndicale de l'éducation et le gouvernement », a-t-il rappelé avant de déclarer que le chef du gouvernement a été réceptif. ​« Heureusement, Monsieur le Premier ministre a été réceptif à nos préoccupations en tant que garant moral du dialogue social en République de Guinée. Il a donné des instructions aux départements sectoriels concernés par l'application des points en souffrance dans le protocole d'accord du 3 janvier 2026, à l'effet de nous rencontrer dans les jours à venir, pour que nous puissions ensemble, rapprocher les positions. » ​Pas de blocage irréversible, mais un « problème d'interprétation sémantique » ​Rassuré par l'écoute du chef du gouvernement, le leader du SNE insiste sur le fait que le différend actuel ne relève pas d'un refus de dialoguer, mais d'une divergence de lecture sur la mise en œuvre du protocole d'accord : ​« Dans son analyse, que nous avons approuvée, il n'y a pas de logique de confrontation entre nous, il y a une logique d'interprétation des points inscrits dans ce protocole. Donc il y a un problème d'interprétation sémantique des mots et des expressions. Et donc cela ne peut pas nous permettre de remettre en cause tout ce qui a été fait déjà. C'est la raison pour laquelle nous allons nous asseoir, discuter de tous les points ». Les parties sont conviées donc à une rencontre le lundi 28 septembre 2026 au Ministère de la Modernisation de l'Administration et de la Fonction Publique.

items.title: Daily Insight for CEOs: Building customer-centric leadership
items.description: Insight. Customer-centric organisations do not simply respond to customers; they design their strategies and operations around the value customers seek. CEOs play a crucial role in ensuring that customer insight reaches the boardroom and influences major decisions. When customer priorities are understood across the organisation, teams can align products, operations, technology, and service around a common objective: creating meaningful customer value. Key Strategies: Bring customer insights into strategic planning. Connect teams to customer outcomes. Measure customer experience consistently. Empower employees to solve customer problems. Use feedback to improve continuously. CEO Leadership Actions. Review customer experience indicators. Discuss customer insights during executive meetings. Encourage leaders to spend time with customers. Actionable Tip. Personally review one customer complaint or service failure and ask what it reveals about the organisation. Why This Matters? Customer-centric leadership strengthens loyalty, innovation, reputation, and sustainable business growth. About the Author. Ernest De-Graft Egyir, CEO advisor, Thought Leader and Founding CEO of Chief Executives Network Ghana, convenes the Ghana CEO Summit and served on Ghana’s Economic Dialogue Planning Committee.

items.title: Democracy must deliver food, jobs and healthcare, not just elections – Mahama
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has said democracy must be judged not only by the conduct of elections but also by its ability to improve the living conditions of citizens. Addressing the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, President Mahama said democratic governance would lose meaning if citizens did not experience tangible improvements in their daily lives. “I have always believed that democracy must deliver tangible social benefits,” he said. “Citizens must experience democracy not only through the ballot box every four years, but through improved access to food, quality education, decent housing, accessible healthcare, and economic opportunity.” He said democratic governments had a responsibility to ensure that political freedoms were accompanied by opportunities for citizens to improve their livelihoods. President Mahama linked the principle to Ghana’s development agenda, saying investments in infrastructure, healthcare, education, social protection and economic opportunities were necessary to make democracy meaningful to ordinary people. He said the strength of a democratic system ultimately depended on whether citizens could see a connection between the institutions they elect and improvements in their everyday lives.

items.title: Capacity constraints must never be a barrier to restitution – Mahama
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has rejected arguments that African countries should first develop modern museums and conservation facilities before cultural artefacts taken during colonial rule are returned. According to the President, concerns about Africa’s capacity to preserve returned heritage should not be used to justify the continued possession of African cultural property by institutions abroad. “Capacity constraints must never be used as a justification for continued possession. Capacity must serve as a bridge to return, not a barrier to justice,” he said at a high-level side event at the United Nations General Assembly on Thursday, September 24. President Mahama said African countries were already developing institutions and infrastructure capable of receiving, preserving and researching returned cultural treasures. He pointed to the African Union’s plans for the Great African Museum, the AU-EU Museum Partnership and Ghana’s own efforts to strengthen national and traditional institutions as evidence of the continent’s commitment to preserving its heritage. He called for international partners to support African countries with technology, conservation expertise, digitisation and professional training rather than using capacity limitations to delay restitution.

items.title: COMAC pushes for suspension of sections of Customs Act 2026
items.description: The Chamber of Oil Marketing Companies (COMAC) is calling for the suspension of sections of the Customs Act 2026 by the Ghana Revenue Authority, over the lack of industry consultation. According to COMAC, it is not in favor of Section 136 of the act that seeks to transfer the entire downstream petroleum tax obligation from oil and LPG Marketing Companies to the Bulk Import, Distribution and Export Companies (BIDECs). It pointed out that “This far-reaching change was introduced without due consultation and presents dire consequences for operators, the industry, and the national economy”. These concerns were captured in a letter to the Commissioner General of the Ghana Revenue Authority, Anothony Kwesi Sarpong, seen by JOYBUSINESS. Reasons for I ndefinite S uspension COMAC, in a letter went ahead to argue that it is kicking against the implementation of the sections of the Customs Act due to the fact that Section 136(3) requires a BIDEC to account for tax at the point of sale, while section 136(5) permits the Commissioner-General (CG) to defer payment for up to 21 days via a bank guarantee. The Chamber went ahead to state that “It migrates liability currently secured by OMC/LPGMC guarantees, bonds, and self-recognisance to the bulk-supply tier.” It recalled at the meeting that GRA’s rationale to deal with “fewer entities” and address marketer defaults was unsupported by any memorandum or assessment, highlighting that this stated rationale is flawed. It also raised serious concerns about enforcing the act, arguing that the current system is effective when enforced. “GRA would face an impossible choice: enforce and trigger a national supply shock, or forbear and allow arrears to balloon. Risk becomes concentrated, not reduced”. Breakdown of O ther C oncerns COMAC went ahead to identify other issues that it believes should be seriously considered. They are: I ssue of enforcement, not the collection point: According to COMAC, the accumulation of arrears points to failures in enforcing existing ICUMS controls, including system overrides that allowed affected operators to continue lifting beyond approved limits. Thus, transferring the tax obligation to BIDECs will merely relocate this risk. C reat ion of fiscal distortion and double collateralisation: It said t he status quo matches liability to liquidity – BIDECs pay at importation, OMCs/LPGMCs pay ex-pump. Section 136 severs this. As a result, BIDEC must pre-finance taxes before being paid, forcing tighter credit, higher security demands, and ultimately higher pump prices. Lack of consultation: It explained thatCOMAC, the body representing the most affected operators, was neither consulted nor invited to comment before passage, despite standing engagement with GRA, NPA, and the Ministries of Finance and Energy. Hence, a post-passage implementation meeting does not cure this procedural defect. Internal inconsistency: It stressed that Section 126(6) fixes the tax point at 21 days after close of a lifting window, while Section 136 fixes it at time of sale with a separate 21-day deferral, two conflicting triggers for the same consignment. This means that no impact assessment, memorandum, transitional plan or financing arrangement has been provided for reference by COMAC. Immediate Attention The Chamber also highlighted some issues that need urgent attention. It expressed concerns about maintenance of the status quo, whereby BIDECs pay at importation (import duties/port charges) and OMCs/LPGMCs continue to account for taxes/levies at ex-pump. Again, it noted about a written account of the control circumstances that permitted affected operators to continue lifting after exceeding the applicable credit limits or payment periods, together with the corrective measures instituted to prevent recurrence; Additionally, an independent review of the grant of non-bonded status and other material system overrides, including the applicable criteria, approval authority, supporting justification, and audit trail, with appropriate administrative or disciplinary action where any breach is established. Plan to Support GRA Despite these concerns, COMAC remains supportive of the GRA and welcomes aspects of the Customs Act. “COMAC remains a willing partner in strengthening compliance and revenue mobilisation, best achieved by enforcing the existing mechanism rather than replacing it”, it explained “We stand ready to engage constructively toward a shared resolution to safeguard our members and national energy security”, it added In conclusion, it welcomed Act 1179 and Sections 126 and 127, which preserve the customs-controlled framework for registration of petroleum operators and bonded storage, lifting, and movement of products.

items.title: 81ᵉ assemblée générale de l’ONU, quelles urgences pour le Sahel ?
items.description: La 81ᵉ session de l'Assemblee generale des Nations unies reunit a New York les dirigeants du monde. Le debat general de haut niveau s'est ouvert le 22 septembre, avec plusieurs enjeux internationaux au programme. Parmi eux, la situation au Sahel. Pour l'analyste politique et enseignant a la faculte des sciences techniques Pierre Claver Bakoroba Traore, l'un des principaux defis consiste a mieux comprendre les soutiens dont beneficient les groupes armes qui destabilisent plusieurs pays de la region. Selon l'enseignent chercheur, les discussions internationales devraient notamment permettre d'identifier les etats qui apportent un soutien aux groupes armes actifs au Sahel. Il estime qu'une reponse collective doit etre recherchee pour eviter que la confrontation militaire ne demeure la seule voie. « Les urgences pour le Sahel, dans le meilleur des mondes, ce serait d'identifier les etats qui amenent le soutien aux groupes qui, aujourd'hui, mettent en difficulte les gouvernements des pays du Sahel », affirme Pierre Claver Bakoroba Traore. L'analyste appelle ainsi a privilegier le dialogue et la recherche de solutions communes. Pour lui, l'Assemblee generale de l'ONU pourrait constituer un cadre permettant aux differents acteurs d'aborder ouvertement la crise sahelienne. Lire aussi : Forum humanitaire de l'AES : du secours d'urgence a des solutions durables Privilegier le dialogue Pierre Claver Bakoroba Traore estime qu'un debat « reellement ouvert et franc » sur la situation au Sahel pourrait contribuer a reduire les tensions. Il considere que les discussions internationales peuvent notamment favoriser un apaisement, voire contribuer a une sortie de crise. « On peut aboutir eventuellement a un apaisement de la crise ou meme eventuellement a la fin de la crise », soutient-il. Au-dela des questions securitaires, l'analyste insiste egalement sur la necessite de s'attaquer « aux problemes de gouvernance dans les pays du Sahel. » Selon lui, l'amelioration de la gouvernance constitue un autre enjeu majeur pour repondre durablement aux crises que connaît la region. Visionnez l'integralite de ce grand dialogue : Senegal-Mali : du soutien « indefectible » aux actes concrets. Quel partenariat pour faire face au terrorisme au Sahel ? L’article 81ᵉ assemblée générale de l’ONU, quelles urgences pour le Sahel ? est apparu en premier sur Studio Tamani - Informations, débats, magazines : toute l’actualité du Mali, en 5 langues .
