items.title: Court is being too ‘high-handed’ by keeping Salomey Awiti Baffoe in custody – Criminologist
items.description: The High Court’s decision to deny bail to Salomey Awiti Baffoe has been criticised by criminologist and lecturer at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), Dr Jones Opoku-Ware, who described the continued detention as “high-handedness.” The court on Thursday, September 24, refused a bail application filed on behalf of the 40-year-old Senior Nursing Officer from Techiman after the prosecution opposed her release. The prosecution argued that Ms Baffoe is still needed to assist with ongoing investigations into the case, which is linked to the high-profile “Ghana Jollof” TikTok controversy. In its ruling, the court said the investigation is cyber-related and that releasing Ms Baffoe at this stage could create a real risk of interference with witnesses. It subsequently directed the Republic to expedite its investigations. Reacting to the ruling on JoyNews’ The Pulse on Thursday, Dr Jones Opoku-Ware said he disagreed with the court’s decision, particularly because the offence is a misdemeanour. “I want to disagree with the court because I feel that for whatever it is worth, this is not the kind of crime that this lady should be held even beyond the mandatory 48-hour period,” he said. He argued that suspects facing misdemeanour charges should ordinarily be considered for bail, rather than being kept in custody for prolonged periods. “How much more misdemeanour crimes?” he asked. Dr Jones Opoku-Ware said the continued detention of Ms Baffoe amounted to what he described as excessive use of state power. “I feel that the lady is being handed too much of high-handedness, and we have to be very careful about the way we are applying the law,” he stated. He urged the authorities to ensure that the law is applied fairly and that the rights of citizens are respected in the handling of criminal cases. “I totally disagree with the position of the court,” he added.

items.title: Tchaoudjo : L’AGDJ offre 120 tables-bancs à cinq établissements scolaires
items.description: Sokodé, 24 sept. (ATOP) – L’Association grandir dans la joie (AGDJ) a offert, le mercredi 23 septembre à Sokodé, 120 tables-bancs à cinq établissements scolaires du primaire de Tchaoudjo. Les Ecoles primaires publiques (EPP) de KpalouKpalou, Komah 2D, Aguidagbadè et Aléhéridè bénéficient de 25 tables-bancs chacune tandis que celle de Bouroda a reçu 20. Ces établissements scolaires sont répartis dans les communes Tchaoudjo 1, 3 et 4. Ce don vise à améliorer les conditions d’apprentissage des élèves en leur offrant un environnement d’étude digne, confortable et propice à la concentration. Il est rendu possible, avec l’appui financier de la Fondation NAK Humanitas. Les tables-bancs ont été réceptionnés par le 1 er adjoint au maire de la commune Tchaoudjo 1, Yérima Agregna qui les a remis, à son tour aux directeurs d’écoles. Le conseiller technique de AGDJ, Elégbédé Franck a indiqué que cette action permet de répondre aux besoins en mobiliers scolaires constatés dans les établissements bénéficiaires, particulièrement en cette période de rentrée scolaire. « Une étude de terrain a révélé une insuffisance de ce mobilier obligeant certains élèves à s’asseoir à plusieurs sur un table-banc », a-t-il ajouté. M. Yérima Agregna a remercié l’association et son partenaire pour ce soutien qui vient accompagner les actions de la municipalité en faveur de l’éducation pour le meilleur devenir des apprenants. « Investir dans l’éducation, c’est contribuer à construire l’avenir de nos enfants», a laissé entendre le 1 er adjoint au maire de la commune Tchaoudjo 1. Le chef division vie scolaire, Boukare Labanté s’est réjoui de cette initiative qui vient en appui à la politique gouvernementale d’éducation de qualité pour tous. Il a promis, au nom des bénéficiaires, de faire un bon usage de ces table-bancs dans l’intérêt supérieur des apprenants d’aujourd’hui et de demain. La cérémonie de remise s’est déroulée en présence des maires des communes concernées, des inspecteurs et directeurs d’établissements. L’Association Grandir dans la Joie est créée en 2019. Elle œuvre, notamment dans les domaines de l’éducation, de l’inclusion sociale, de l’accompagnement des enfants vulnérables et du développement communautaire. ATOP/TAA/MEK/SED

items.title: La Guinée-Bissau célèbre le 53ᵉ anniversaire de son indépendance du Portugal
items.description: La Republique de Guinee-Bissau celebre sa fete nationale ce 24 septembre, marquant la 53ᵉ commemoration de son independance reconnue par le Portugal le 10 septembre 1974, apres la revolution des Œillets survenue a Lisbonne. Le pays a cependant retenu cette date comme jour officiel de commemoration, puisqu'elle correspond a la proclamation unilaterale de 1973. Traditionnellement, l'occasion est marquee par des ceremonies officielles, des discours, des spectacles culturels, de la musique, des danses traditionnelles et des celebrations publiques. C'est aussi l'occasion pour les Bissau-guineens de se pencher sur leur histoire et sur les sacrifices consentis durant la lutte pour l'accession a l'independance, explique la presse locale. La Guinée-Bissau célèbre 53 ans d’indépendance et se tourne vers de nouvelles perspectives. Avec 1,95 million USD engagé dans les télécommunications, la BIDC soutient une meilleure connectivité et contribue à ouvrir de nouvelles voies au progrès économique et social du pays. pic.twitter.com/lZDaa33nPU — ECOWAS Bank for Investment and Development (EBID) (@BIDC_EBID) September 24, 2026 Le parcours vers l'independance de la Guinee-Bissau La lutte pour l'independance de la Guinee-Bissau du joug colonial portugais demarre en 1956 sous l'impulsion d'Amílcar Cabral et Rafael Paula Barbosa qui fonderent clandestinement le Parti africain pour l'independance de la Guinee et du Cap-Vert (PAIGC). D'abord pacifique, la lutte deviendra armee des 1961 pour reconquerir jusqu'a 70 % du territoire en 1968. Le PAIGC reussit sa bataille diplomatique au sein de l'ONU qui vote la resolution 3061 a l'Assemblee generale reconnaissant l'independance de la Guinee-Bissau et condamnant la politique coloniale du Portugal et ses agressions contre le peuple bissau-guineen. S'ensuivent alors des negociations a Londres puis a Alger qui se denoueront par une declaration conjointe, presentee le 26 août, dans laquelle le Portugal s'engage a reconnaître officiellement la Republique de Guinee-Bissau le 10 septembre suivant et a proceder, avant le 31 octobre, au retrait de toutes les forces armees portugaises du pays. La Guinee-Bissau a ete le theâtre d'un coup d'etat mene le 26 novembre 2025 par le « Haut commandement militaire pour la restauration de la securite nationale et de l'ordre public », qui a renverse le president Umaro Sissoco Embaló, actuellement en exil, et installe le general Horta N'Tam, chef d'etat-major de l'armee de terre, a la tete du pays pour une periode de transition d'un an.

items.title: 152e réunion du conseil d’administration de la BOAD : Plusieurs dossiers soumis à l’approbation des administrateurs
items.description: Lomé, 24 sept. (ATOP) – Plusieurs dossiers sont soumis aux administrateurs et administratrices de la Banque ouest africaine de développement (BOAD) réunis, le jeudi 24 septembre à Lomé, pour la 152 e réunion du conseil d’administration de cette institution sous-régionale. « Nous procéderons à l’arrêt des comptes intermédiaires de la Banque au 30 juin 2026 et prendre connaissance du compte-rendu de la 54 e réunion du comité d’audit de la banque », a annoncé le président de la BOAD, Serge Ekue à l’ouverture des travaux. Les dossiers soumis à l’approbation des participants, dit-il, sont inscrits dans une logique de rigueur et d’impact. Ces dossiers concernent les secteurs stratégiques, la mécanisation agricole, les investissements, les infrastructures routières et aéroportuaires, la production de ciment, les projets et opérations dans le secteur de l’énergie, un secteur éminemment stratégique. Outre ces interventions structurelles, les administrateurs auront à plancher sur un programme d’urgence dédié à la résilience agricole et énergétique. Pour soutenir la dynamique et les ambitions du « Plan Djoliba… La suite, 2026-2030 », poursuit M. Ekue, nous examinerons également les opportunités de mobilisation de ressources auprès des partenaires, entre autres, l’Agence française de développement, la Banque africaine de développement, la KFW, l’instrument de développement de nos partenaires allemands ainsi que la Banque de développement européenne et la Chine. Le président de la BOAD s’est félicité de la structure financière de la banque au 30 juin 2026, « ce qui confirme l’aspect confortable de notre structure de capital et de nos fonds de propres ». « Mesdames et Messieurs, vous voyez bien notre cap est clair : financer plus, financer mieux, tout en accompagnant les États face aux mutations socio-économiques et sécuritaires de notre région. Tel est le sens de notre action, tel est notre engagement sans cesse renouvelé », a réitéré M. Ekue. « Djoliba… La Suite », le plan stratégique 2026-2030 de la BOAD, ambitionne de porter les financements à 6 500 Mds FCFA, soit le double du plan précédent, avec une approche sectorielle centrée sur l’énergie, l’agriculture, la santé, l’éducation et l’habitat abordable. ATOP/AJA/BV

items.title: Cop martyred, 3 injured as terrorists open fire on raiding CTD party near Peshawar
items.description: PESHAWAR: A cop was martyred and three others were injured on Thursday during an exchange of fire between terrorists and the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) on the outskirts of the provincial capital, police said. According to a senior CTD official, the department had received information about the presence of terrorists in the Garhi Sherdad area near Warsak Road, following which the authorities planned an operation against them. “The moment the CTD team reached the area, the terrorists opened fire at the raiding party,” the official said. In a subsequent post about the raid, KP Police said one CTD personnel embraced martyrdom, while three were injured in exchange of fire. “In retaliatory action, one terrorist [was] killed,” the statement added, highlighting that a “major terrorist plot” was foiled. The police said the operation was carried out on “credible intel” about the presence of three would-be suicide bombers. A video, captured by a quadcopter camera, purportedly showed one of the terrorists climbing from a house and making his way to another, running along the rooftops. The terrorist, who succeeded in climbing up to the main door of the third house, was targeted right on top of the wall by the CTD personnel who had cordoned off the entire area. The funeral of the martyred cop, Afaaq Khan, was offered at Peshawar’s police headquarters. KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi, cabinet members, KP Inspector General Zulfiqar Hameed, Additional IG CTD Jawad Qamar, Peshawar Capital City Police Officer (CCPO) Dr Mian Saeed Ahmad, and relatives of the martyred cop attended the funeral. In a statement, Kundi strongly condemned the incident, expressed his condolences to the family of the martyred official and prayed for the swift recovery of the injured. “The people of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa remain deeply indebted to these brave sons of our soil who put their lives on the line so that others may live in safety,” he said. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has witnessed an increase in terrorist activity in recent months, with LEAs and security forces being targeted, prompting authorities to intensify counterterrorism operations. Earlier this month, five terrorists were killed in an exchange of fire with CTD of police in Shamshatoo area on the border between Peshawar and Nowshera districts. Among them was a key commander of the banned ISKP, identified as Imran alias Abdullah alias Bilal alias Abu Bakar, police said. It added that Imran was a proclaimed offender wanted by CTD as he was involved in a total of 20 cases of bomb blasts, targeted killings of police personnel and political leaders, and other acts of terrorism in Islamabad and other parts of the country. A week before that, four terrorists, including a militant commander and an Afghan national, were killed in an encounter with CTD in Peshawar’s Badhber area. A statement issued by CTD said that earlier, militant commander Tahir alias Muawiya, a resident of Shakas in Khyber tribal district, along with his other associates, was seen roaming the area to challenge the writ of the government.

items.title: Lawyer for Salomey Baffoe appeals bail refusal, petitions CJ to intervene
items.description: Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah, the defence lawyer for the nurse standing trial for allegedly abetting the publication of false news in connection with the “Ghana Jollof” saga, has announced plans to appeal the High Court’s decision to decline bail for his client. The Accra High Court refused an application for bail on Thursday, September 24, filed on behalf of Salomey Awiti Baffoe after the prosecution opposed her release, arguing that she was still needed to assist with ongoing investigations. The defence has also indicated that it will petition the Chief Justice to allow the Court of Appeal to sit, where necessary, to deal with the matter concerning Ms Baffoe’s liberty. The court, in its decision, held that the investigation was cyber-related and that releasing Ms Baffoe posed a real risk of interference with witnesses. However, her defence lawyer has challenged the basis for the continued detention, arguing that the police charge sheet indicates that investigations concerning Ms Baffoe herself have been completed. Speaking to the media after the ruling, Nana Agyei Baffour said the remaining investigations were focused on third parties allegedly involved in the redistribution of videos. “Per the charge sheet, what is outstanding is rather the search for third parties who are alleged to have done the redistribution of the videos.” Nana Agyei Baffour also questioned how Ms Baffoe could interfere with information when her mobile phones had already been seized by the police. “In terms of deletion, how is Madam Salomey Awiti Baffoe in a position to delete information?” He said the police had already taken possession of her phones and, according to statements made by the police, had accessed them and reached certain findings. “Per her own assertion, they have already gone into her phone and have established or made certain findings.” The defence, however, disputed the circumstances surrounding the alleged examination of the phone, arguing that if the police had accessed the device, it was done without the presence or knowledge of counsel or Ms Baffoe’s consent. Although the lawyers said they respected the High Court’s decision, counsel maintained that the court had failed to adequately consider what he described as vital documentary evidence before it. “What is obvious is that the court exercised its discretion without considering very vital materials before it.” He said this was the reason the defence disagreed with the ruling and had decided to challenge it. “That is why we disagree with the decision, even though we respect it.” Nana Agyei Baffour said the family had instructed the legal team to take all necessary legal steps to secure Ms Baffoe’s liberty. “I’ve been instructed by the family to proceed to ensure that the liberty of the mother of three minor children is secured.” He confirmed that an appeal would be filed against the High Court’s decision. “We are proceeding by filing an appeal against the decision of the High Court.” Lawyers petition Chief Justice In addition to filing the appeal, the defence intends to petition the Chief Justice to facilitate an expedited hearing before the Court of Appeal. Nana Agyei Baffour said the petition would seek permission for the appellate court to sit where necessary, particularly given that the matter concerns the liberty of an individual. He explained that the defence would seek the intervention of the Chief Justice in the same way that courts may, in exceptional circumstances, be allowed to sit during vacation to deal with urgent matters. “We are also going to petition the Lord Chief Justice that, just as in exceptional or very exceptional circumstances, it allows the Supreme Court to even sit during vacations; once it concerns the liberty of a person, we are petitioning the Chief Justice to let the Court of Appeal sit.” According to counsel, the defence wants the matter expedited once the necessary court record is transmitted. He said the record was not expected to be voluminous and that the legal team would take steps to ensure the process moves quickly. “We are going to make sure it is expedited because it’s not a voluminous record.” Nana Agyei Baffour also highlighted the effect of Ms Baffoe’s detention on her three minor children. He said the children continued to ask about the whereabouts of their mother, with particular concern over her 15-year-old child. According to the lawyer, the teenager has remained at home and has not been able to join his peers in Form One as he transitions from basic education to secondary school. The defence says the circumstances have reinforced its decision to pursue the appeal as quickly as possible. “We are going to do everything within our power and our means and in accordance with the law to ensure that the liberty of Madam Salome Awiti Baffoe is secured.” Counsel said the ultimate objective was to secure Ms Baffoe’s release and enable her to reunite with her three children.

items.title: PM Shehbaz meets Iranian President Pezeshkian on UNGA sidelines
items.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Thursday on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York. In a post on the social media platform X, the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said the meeting had begun, adding that the two would discuss Pakistan-Iran relations and the situation in the region. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, and Special Assistant to the Prime Minister Tariq Fatemi are also present at the meeting, as well as Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, the PMO said. The two leaders had previously held a meeting in Kyrgyzstan, on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Council of Heads of State meeting in August, during which they reaffirmed the close and longstanding ties between both countries. At the same time, PM Shehbaz had also stressed the importance of restraint and sustained diplomatic engagement to achieve lasting peace and stability in the region amid the US-Iran conflict. Thursday’s meeting with the Iranian president comes as Islamabad continues efforts to bring the United States and Iran back to the negotiating table regarding the war in the Middle East. Pezeshkian on Wednesday struck a defiant tone speaking at the UN for the first time since Washington and Israel launched an all-out war on his country, vowing Tehran would never “bend at the knee”. He made no reference to the talks to resolve the stalled war in his steely speech. However, the Iranian side earlier this week indicated its willingness to return to dialogue with the US to de-escalate tensions. The flexibility on the issue was indicated by the Iranian side in a meeting between Pezeshkian and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi during the latter’s visit to Tehran. The latest diplomatic activity follows the collapse of the 14-point Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding brokered by Pakistan on June 17. The conflict has since continued with sporadic strikes and a US naval blockade of Iranian ports, while Iran has maintained control over traffic through the strategic waterway. Pakistan, meanwhile, has remained engaged in efforts to keep the diplomatic channel open. Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir has used his contacts with the US administration, while Pakistani officials have made repeated visits to Tehran. Diplomatic sources say Qatar is handling the immediate shuttle diplomacy between the US and Iran in New York, while Pakistan is working through a parallel channel with Tehran as regional efforts intensify to keep the latest diplomatic contacts from collapsing. The distinction has emerged from reporting by US and international media on the renewed US-Iran contacts around the United Nations General Assembly, with Qatar and Pakistan both involved in efforts to keep communication open between Washington and Tehran. PM Shehbaz is expected to address the UNGA on Friday.

items.title: Défense russe : la libération de Dobropolié renforce l’avancée russe et accroît la pression sur les positions ukrainiennes dans le Donbass
items.description: Le ministere russe de la Defense a indique, le 24 septembre, que les unites du groupement de troupes « Centre » poursuivaient leurs operations a Dobropolie, ou un regiment ukrainien est encercle. Alors que les troupes russes developpent leur offensive en direction d'Alexandrovka, les attaques ukrainiennes et les tentatives visant a rompre l'encerclement sont repoussees. La situation autour de Dobropolie revet une importance particuliere pour la suite des operations russes dans cette partie du front. Le ministere russe de la Defense considere la ville comme une importante zone fortifiee, utilisee par les forces ukrainiennes pour frapper le flanc et l'arriere du groupement de troupes « Sud », engage dans son avancee vers Droujkovka. La maîtrise des hauteurs autour de la ville constitue egalement un element important pour la progression russe. Selon le ministere, leur controle permettrait d'accelerer l'avancee des troupes vers les limites administratives de la Republique populaire de Donetsk et de renforcer leur position sur cet axe. Un point cle pour la logistique ukrainienne L'importance de Dobropolie ne se limite pas a sa position militaire. La ville constitue egalement un nœud de transport relie a la region de Dnipropetrovsk, par lequel passe l'une des principales voies d'approvisionnement des forces ukrainiennes. Sa liberation pourrait ainsi avoir des consequences plus larges sur le dispositif ukrainien dans le Donbass. Le ministere russe affirme que la maîtrise de la ville ne perturberait pas seulement certains itineraires, mais « toute la chaîne logistique » alimentant les unites ukrainiennes dans la region. C'est dans ce contexte que le ministere russe de la Defense considere l'axe de Dobropolie comme « l'un des secteurs cles » pour la poursuite des operations. Le controle de la ville et des hauteurs environnantes doit faciliter la progression russe tout en accentuant la pression sur les positions ukrainiennes plus en profondeur dans le Donbass. Les tentatives ukrainiennes pour rompre l'encerclement sont repoussees L'importance du secteur explique egalement les tentatives des forces ukrainiennes pour degager le groupement encercle, tout en cherchant a empecher les troupes russes d'achever la prise du secteur. Les attaques menees dans cette zone ainsi que les tentatives de sortie de l'encerclement sont repoussees, indique le ministere. Ces combats s'accompagnent, selon les autorites militaires russes, de pertes importantes dans les rangs ukrainiens. Le ministere estime qu'entre 30 et 50 militaires ukrainiens sont tues chaque jour dans le secteur de Dobropolie. Au-dela de la situation locale, la liberation de Dobropolie aurait enfin une portee plus large pour la suite des operations dans le Donbass. Selon le ministere russe de la Defense, elle renforcerait la pression sur l'agglomeration Slaviansk-Kramatorsk-Droujkovka, consideree comme le principal ensemble fortifie des forces ukrainiennes dans la region.

items.title: Court upholds sentence against Omnia Sweidan for publishing description of obstetric violence at Al-Shatby Hospital
items.description: Omnia Sweidan’s appeal against a fine and prison sentence she received for a Facebook post describing abuses against patients was rejected on Thursday, according to her lawyer Ahmed Ragheb. Sweidan was tried earlier this year on charges relating to the post which detailed obstetric and other forms of violence against women at Alexandria’s Al-Shatby Hospital. A misdemeanor court ultimately issued her with a six-month prison sentence and a LE20,000 fine. The prison sentence was issued with a three-year suspension. Ragheb told Mada Masr that after he attended her hearing at the Economic Misdemeanors Court at Dekheila Courthouse this week, the court rejected her appeal and upheld the July ruling. Sweidan’s post described instances of physical and sexual abuse of women patients at Alexandria University’s Al-Shatby Hospital. Sweidan recounted incidents she said she had witnessed or heard discussed during her medical training in the hospital’s obstetrics and gynecology department six years earlier. The post went viral within hours and drew tens of thousands of shares and comments amid a conversation that quickly turned to other instances of obstetric violence, with many women sharing their own experiences of mistreatment in maternity wards. Healthcare professionals who spoke to Mada Masr said the abuses she recounted reflected a common and pervasive reality in public hospitals. The head of legal affairs at Alexandria University Hospitals subsequently filed a complaint against Sweidan, citing concerns over the hospitals’ reputation. Sweidan was arrested from her home in Damanhour on June 16, one day after publishing the testimony, and was later released on LE20,000 bail following questioning by prosecutors. The prosecution subsequently referred her to the Economic Misdemeanors Court on charges of deliberately broadcasting false news, using an electronic account to commit a crime and publishing false news. The misdemeanor court ultimately convicted Sweidan in June on the charges of publishing false news and intentionally spreading false news, while acquitting her at the same time on a separate charge of using a social media account to commit a crime. The court also excluded a provision of the cybercrime law concerning violations of Egyptian family values from the case. The post Court upholds sentence against Omnia Sweidan for publishing description of obstetric violence at Al-Shatby Hospital first appeared on Mada Masr .

items.title: Washington State delegation explores healthcare partnership with Ghana Medical Trust Fund
items.description: A delegation from Washington State in the United States has paid a courtesy call on the Ghana Medical Trust Fund (GMTF) to explore opportunities for partnership and collaboration in healthcare delivery. The delegation, led by Mayor of Shoreline, Washington, Betsy Robertson, engaged the management of the Fund on areas of mutual interest, particularly efforts to strengthen healthcare delivery and improve access to specialised medical services in Ghana. The visit forms part of broader efforts to establish strategic partnerships that can support the GMTF’s mandate of expanding access to quality healthcare and improving outcomes for patients across the country. Discussions focused on identifying practical areas where collaboration could contribute to Ghana’s healthcare needs. The GMTF management, led by Administrator Adjoa Obuobia Darko-Opoku, welcomed the delegation and expressed the Fund’s readiness to explore practical areas of cooperation. The Fund said such partnerships could help mobilise expertise and resources towards initiatives capable of delivering meaningful impact to Ghana’s healthcare system.

items.title: BoG backs cedi payments for Ghana-China trade
items.description: The Bank of Ghana (BoG) says it is supporting efforts to facilitate trade between Ghana and China using the cedi, as part of measures to reduce reliance on the US dollar for bilateral transactions. Governor of the Bank of Ghana, Dr Johnson Pandit Asiama, said banks are already piloting arrangements that will allow Ghanaian importers to make payments for goods from China in Ghana cedis. He was speaking at the 132nd Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) press briefing. According to Dr Asiama, Stanbic Bank is currently piloting a programme under which importers no longer have to source US dollars to make payments for their imports from China. “As we speak, if you want to buy anything from China, just go to Stanbic Bank with your cedis. You are able to do that,” he said. He added that Ghana Commercial Bank is also working on a similar arrangement as the country seeks to deepen financial and trade links with China. The Governor said the Bank of Ghana is taking the development seriously in view of the growing trade relationship between the two countries. He further indicated that the central bank will engage its counterparts in China on opportunities arising from the zero-tariff policy regime, while the Ministry of Trade will also have a role to play in ensuring Ghana takes full advantage of the development. “As the central bank, we’re doing a number of things,” Dr Asiama said, adding that the Bank will continue to work with relevant institutions to support the growing Ghana-China trade relationship. The move forms part of broader efforts to facilitate cross-border payments and reduce the need for businesses engaged in Ghana-China trade to rely solely on the US dollar for transactions.

items.title: Dakar 2026, l’autre épreuve des Jeux (Par Atoumane Traoré)
items.description: Du 31 octobre au 13 novembre 2026, il y aura les chronomètres, les podiums, les drapeaux et cette jeunesse venue du monde entier qui donnera à Dakar les couleurs de l’Olympisme. Pour la première fois, un événement olympique se tiendra sur le continent africain. Il faut mesurer ce que cela signifie. Dakar accueille. L’Afrique célèbre. Le monde regarde. Pendant deux semaines, le Sénégal bénéficiera d’une exposition internationale exceptionnelle. Des athlètes, des délégations, des responsables, des entreprises, des médias et des visiteurs convergeront vers un même territoire. Avec eux circuleront des données, des technologies, des capitaux, des informations et des intérêts. Dakar 2026 sera une fête sportive. Ce sera aussi, qu’on le veuille ou non, un moment stratégique. Car les grands événements internationaux ont changé de nature. Leur sécurité ne se joue plus seulement aux abords des stades. Il faudra naturellement protéger les sites, les délégations, les déplacements et les populations, prévenir la menace terroriste, organiser les secours et préparer la gestion de crise. Mais une enceinte peut être parfaitement surveillée tandis que l’événement est atteint ailleurs. Une cyberattaque peut interrompre un service essentiel. Une défaillance des télécommunications peut désorganiser plusieurs fonctions. Un prestataire compromis peut ouvrir un accès à un système sensible. Une fuite d’informations peut exposer un dispositif. Une manipulation numérique peut transformer un incident limité en crise d’ampleur internationale. Le terrorisme lui-même a investi l’espace numérique. On y recrute, on y observe, on y collecte de l’information, on y intimide. L’espionnage, lui aussi, a changé de terrain. Il ne recherche plus seulement des secrets. Il s’intéresse aux données, aux technologies, aux réseaux humains, aux organisations, aux accès et aux vulnérabilités. Un grand événement mondial constitue un formidable espace de rencontres. Il devient, par la même occasion, un espace d’observation et de collecte. Le reconnaître ne relève pas de l’alarmisme. C’est regarder le monde tel qu’il est devenu. Dakar 2026 impose dès lors une question simple. De quoi dépendra réellement le fonctionnement des Jeux ? Derrière les compétitions existe une architecture invisible faite d’électricité, de télécommunications, de transports, de systèmes d’information, de paiements, de centres de données, d’équipements et de prestataires. Nous savons généralement identifier ce qui est important. Nous connaissons moins bien ce qui relie ces éléments entre eux. Or une technologie peut dépendre d’un fournisseur unique. Un service essentiel peut reposer sur un équipement difficilement remplaçable. Plusieurs opérateurs peuvent dépendre d’une même infrastructure. Une entreprise apparemment secondaire peut détenir des accès déterminants. Le danger n’est pas toujours là où l’on regarde. Il se trouve parfois dans ce que personne n’avait pensé à regarder. L’intelligence économique trouve ici sa véritable fonction. Elle n’est ni une couche supplémentaire de sécurité ni une technique réservée aux entreprises. Elle est une manière de comprendre son environnement, ses intérêts, ses rapports de force et ses dépendances pour mieux anticiper. Cette lecture concerne aussi l’économie. Les Jeux feront circuler des investissements, créeront des marchés et mobiliseront l’hôtellerie, les transports, les télécommunications, la restauration, le tourisme, les services numériques et de nombreuses entreprises. Mais le véritable bilan économique commencera après la cérémonie de clôture. Quelle part de la valeur créée sera restée au Sénégal ? Quelles entreprises nationales auront grandi ? Quels savoir-faire auront été acquis ? Quelles compétences auront été transférées ? Quels investissements continueront à produire leurs effets ? Les Jeux révéleront également ce que nous ne maîtrisons pas encore. Les technologies qu’il faudra importer, les compétences recherchées à l’extérieur, les équipements dont nous dépendons dessineront en creux une partie de notre vulnérabilité économique et technologique. Il faudra savoir regarder cette réalité sans complexe. La souveraineté ne consiste pas à tout produire soi-même. Elle commence par la connaissance de ses dépendances et par la capacité de distinguer celles que l’on peut accepter de celles qu’il faut réduire, diversifier ou sécuriser. Dakar 2026 sera enfin une bataille de l’information. Jamais un événement de cette importance ne s’est déroulé dans un environnement où une image, une rumeur ou une fausse alerte peuvent atteindre plusieurs millions de personnes en quelques minutes. L’intelligence artificielle permet désormais de fabriquer des images, des voix et des récits dont la vraisemblance rend la manipulation plus redoutable encore. Une information fausse peut précéder la vérité. Un incident mineur peut devenir mondial. Une opération organisée peut chercher non pas à perturber directement les Jeux, mais à atteindre la confiance qu’ils inspirent. Et la confiance a une valeur. L’image laissée par Dakar 2026 pèsera dans le tourisme, l’investissement, l’attractivité du Sénégal et sa capacité à accueillir demain d’autres grands événements. La responsabilité est d’autant plus forte qu’il s’agit des premiers Jeux olympiques organisés en Afrique. Une réussite sera sénégalaise, mais son retentissement sera africain. Une crise majeure risquerait, elle aussi, d’être racontée au-delà de nos frontières. Il faudra donc protéger une infrastructure que l’on ne peut entourer de barrières, la réputation du pays. Cela ne signifie ni contrôler l’opinion ni imposer un récit. Cela signifie savoir détecter une manipulation, établir rapidement les faits, comprendre sa propagation et répondre avant que le vide ne soit occupé par d’autres. Tout cela suppose enfin une capacité collective. Les nouvelles menaces possèdent un avantage sur nos organisations. Elles ignorent les frontières administratives. Une attaque peut être numérique, produire des conséquences économiques, provoquer une perturbation physique puis devenir une crise d’opinion. Si chaque institution n’en observe qu’une partie, personne ne voit réellement l’ensemble. La maturité du dispositif sénégalais se mesurera donc moins au nombre de structures mobilisées qu’à leur capacité à partager une même compréhension de la situation, détecter les signaux faibles, anticiper, décider et maintenir les fonctions essentielles lorsque survient l’imprévu. C’est peut-être là que réside l’héritage le plus précieux de Dakar 2026. Les Jeux passeront. Les infrastructures resteront. Mais devraient aussi rester les compétences acquises, les entreprises renforcées, les mécanismes de coordination éprouvés, une meilleure connaissance de nos dépendances et une culture plus exigeante de l’anticipation. Le Sénégal n’a aucune raison d’aborder ce rendez-vous avec inquiétude. Il a toutes les raisons de l’aborder avec lucidité. Accueillir le monde est une marque de confiance. Savoir protéger ce que cette ouverture expose est une marque de maturité. Dakar accueille. L’Afrique célèbre. Le monde regarde. Et lorsque le monde regarde, la réussite ne dépend plus seulement de ce qu’on lui donne à voir. Elle dépend aussi de notre capacité à voir ce qu’il ne voit pas. Atoumane TRAORE Spécialiste en gouvernance stratégique, cybersécurité et intelligence économique

items.title: Automobile : l’Algérie n’importera plus de pièces plastiques dès 2027
items.description: L’Algérie a pris une nouvelle mesure radicale dans le domaine de l’industrie automobile afin de pousser les constructeurs automobiles à utiliser des composants fabriqués localement. Pour les équipements automobiles locaux, c’est une décision qui leur garantira un bon carnet de commandes. « Il faut s'éloigner des chiffres creux et de l’assemblage encore plus creux. » La sentence est du Premier ministre Sifi Ghrieb à propos du taux d’intégration de l’industrie automobile en Algérie . Ghrieb a annoncé des mesures concrètes et fixé une deadline ferme aux constructeurs concernant l’utilisation des composants plastiques fabriqués localement. Le Premier ministre s’exprimait ce jeudi 24 septembre à l’occasion de la relance d’une usine de composants plastiques à Tissemsilt, appartenant à la société GPI (Global Plastic Injection) de la holding publique ACS (industries chimiques). Industrie automobile : plus aucun composant plastique ne sera importé à partir de 2027 Le taux d’assemblage commence à augmenter, mais il faut plus pour parler d'une véritable industrie automobile. L’ouverture de l'usine de Tissemsilt est une opportunité pour booster le taux d’intégration. « Plus aucune pièce plastique entrant dans l’industrie automobile qui pourrait être fabriquée chez GPI (Global Plastic Injection) ne sera importée à partir du début de l’année prochaine », a tranché le Premier ministre. Les constructeurs automobiles agréés en Algérie sont tenus de se conformer à cette décision. “D’ici la fin de l'année, je dis bien avant la fin de l’année, les moules de tous les composants plastiques entrant dans l'industrie et le montage automobile seront ici dans cette usine”, a annoncé Sifi Ghrieb dans une déclaration faite au sein de l’usine qu'il venait d'inaugurer. L’usine est exploitée par la société GPI (Global Plastic Injection), relevant du groupe public des spécialités chimiques Holding ACS. “À partir d’aujourd'hui, cette société, GPI, doit avoir un cahier des charges aux contours clairs avec l’ensemble des constructeurs”, a ajouté le Premier ministre qui a mis en garde contre les faux-fuyants qui pourraient être avancés concernant l’importation des moules. “Je connais toutes les chansons des moules (…) que personne ne vienne me dire qu'il faut une année pour importer le moule. Il y a des alternatives”, a-t-il dit. “Personne ne dira : vous m'avez bloqué” Selon Ghrieb, l’État veille à ce qu'il y ait un taux d’intégration effectif. L’Algérie commence à avoir une industrie automobile véritable et “entre dans la chaîne de production avec une haute valeur ajoutée”, a-t-il ajouté. En tout cas, a-t-il insisté, “d’ici la fin de l’année, aucune pièce plastique qui peut être fabriquée ici à Tissemsilt ne sera importée”. “Personne ne dira ‘vous m'avez bloqué’. Vous allez ramener vos moules dès maintenant et je ne laisserai aucun composant plastique rentrer à partir du 31 décembre”, a-t-il répété. La même chose sera faite pour l'usine de carrosseries de Batna qui a été lancée fin avril dernier, a-t-il souligné. L'usine de Tissemsilt pourra aussi fournir les autres secteurs, comme les industries de l'électroménager et de l’électronique, qui utilisent aussi des composants plastiques. Pour lui permettre de couvrir toute la demande, le Premier ministre a annoncé que la nouvelle usine bénéficiera d'investissements supplémentaires et devra atteindre à terme sa pleine capacité de production et fonctionner en 24 heures sur 24. L’article Automobile : l’Algérie n’importera plus de pièces plastiques dès 2027 est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: EPA shuts down Earl International mining operation at Gbane over environmental breaches
items.description: The Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) has ordered Earl International Mining Limited to immediately cease all operations at its underground gold mining and processing facility at Gbane in the Talensi District of the Upper East Region. The directive, contained in a closure notice dated September 22, 2026, follows what the EPA described as the company’s failure to comply with corrective measures outlined in an Enforcement Notice issued in February and a Pre-closure Notice issued in April. The notice, signed by Prof. Michael Ayamga, Acting Deputy Chief Executive Officer in charge of Operations, said the company had continued to operate despite several outstanding environmental compliance issues. According to the EPA, Earl International’s Environmental Permits for its underground gold mining and processing operations and its tailings storage facility expired in February 2023. The Authority said the company is therefore operating without a valid Environmental Permit, contrary to Regulation 3 of the Environmental Protection (Environmental Assessment) Regulations, 2025 (LI 2504). The EPA also said the company had failed to post the required Reclamation Bond for its operations as required under the regulations. The EPA further said Earl International had commenced construction of new underground shafts, an expanded processing plant, a solar farm and staff accommodation without obtaining the requisite environmental approvals. It said the projects were at various stages of completion and that their construction contravened the environmental assessment regulations. The Authority also raised concerns about the company’s continued use of what it described as an un-engineered Tailings Storage Facility (TSF), citing risks to the stability of the facility and possible groundwater contamination. According to the EPA, the TSF has been divided into five cells, with tailings deposition completed in cells one, two and three without the required reclamation measures to control excessive dust. The company is currently depositing tailings into cell four, while cell five is being used as a supernatant pond. The EPA said records indicated that the TSF was constructed without its approval and that the downstream face of the southern embankment of cell four had recently been repaired following what the Authority described as a perceived failure. It also said there was no monitoring instrumentation on the TSF to assess the stability of its embankments. The Authority said Earl International was also discharging underground water into the external environment without establishing the quality and quantity of the discharge. It warned that the practice could adversely affect surface water bodies and contribute to a drawdown of water levels in community boreholes. The EPA said the discharge contravenes the Environmental Protection (Effluent) Regulations, 2025 (LI 2506), and the Ghana Standards for Environment and Health Protection — Requirements for Effluent Discharge (GS 1212:2019). The EPA said it had previously directed Earl International to obtain an environmental permit for an engineered TSF and secure permits for all ongoing projects identified by the Authority. The company was also instructed to install functional monitoring equipment on the TSF embankments, ensure their stability, commission an independent third-party stability assessment and hydrological study, and submit a closure plan for cells one, two and three. It was further directed to implement appropriate underground dewatering measures. The EPA said the company was also required to pay an administrative fee of US$2 million. Following engagements with company representatives, the amount was reduced to US$1 million. However, the Authority said Earl International had failed to comply with the directives, providing grounds for the suspension of its Environmental Permit under Regulation 35 of LI 2504. The Authority also said recent developments suggested that Earl International had failed to adequately protect its concession from illegal mining activities, despite a directive to mining companies to take steps to protect their concessions. The EPA described the situation as posing a serious environmental risk.

items.title: Sonorités traditionnelles d’inspiration islamique : Le CCIB mise sur le patrimoine pour renforcer le vivre-ensemble
items.description: Le Centre culturel islamique du Burkina (CCIB) a officiellement ouvert, ce 24 septembre 2026, les Journées des sonorités traditionnelles d’inspiration islamique pour la paix et le vivre-ensemble. Pendant deux jours, participants, acteurs culturels et religieux réfléchiront à la manière de valoriser le dodo, le tarkaye, les mansés, le salou, le gassid et d’autres expressions culturelles comme leviers de cohésion sociale et de prévention de l’extrémisme violent. Le patrimoine culturel peut-il contribuer à renforcer le vivre-ensemble au Burkina Faso ? C’est autour de cette question que s’articulent les Journées des sonorités traditionnelles d’inspiration islamique pour la paix et le vivre-ensemble. Initiée par le Centre culturel islamique du Burkina (CCIB), cette rencontre entend remettre au centre des échanges des pratiques culturelles qui ont longtemps accompagné la vie sociale des communautés musulmanes burkinabè et favorisé les rencontres entre les différentes composantes de la société. Représentant le ministre en charge de la Culture, le conseiller technique Abdoulaye Dioni a salué une initiative qui intervient dans un contexte marqué par les défis sécuritaires et sociaux auxquels le Burkina Faso est confronté. « Le thème qui nous rassemble touche au cœur même du combat que mène actuellement le Burkina Faso. Un combat militaire, certes, mais aussi et surtout un combat culturel, mémoriel et identitaire » , a-t-il déclaré. Pour lui, les sonorités telles que les mansés, le salou, le tarkaye ou encore le dodo ont historiquement dépassé le cadre du divertissement. Elles constituaient également des espaces de rassemblement et de transmission de valeurs. « Elles étaient le ciment de nos réjouissances, les gardiennes de nos valeurs de solidarité, et des ponts jetés vers les autres composantes de notre société multiethnique et pluriconfessionnelle » , a-t-il souligné. Réhabiliter des pratiques en perte de vitesse Le CCIB constate que plusieurs de ces expressions culturelles sont aujourd’hui moins présentes dans les pratiques sociales. Cette évolution, combinée à certaines dynamiques de repli identitaire et au durcissement des dogmes religieux, contribue à fragiliser les espaces traditionnels de rencontre entre les communautés. C’est dans ce contexte que le centre entend œuvrer à leur réhabilitation. Pour l’imam Alidou Ilboudo, coordonnateur du CCIB, ces journées s’inscrivent dans la continuité du projet « Djama Béog-Néré » , dont le centre porte la composante « Communication et Culture » . Cette composante s’est notamment matérialisée par des émissions radiophoniques et télévisées, ainsi que par des caravanes de sensibilisation consacrées au vivre-ensemble et à la cohésion sociale. « C’est un pas audacieux et concret vers le renforcement de la cohésion sociale » (Imam Alidou Ilboudo) Les travaux s’articulent autour de trois principaux axes. Le premier porte sur le gain social des sonorités traditionnelles et leur capacité à contribuer au vivre-ensemble, à la paix et à la cohésion sociale. Le deuxième concerne les préoccupations théologiques, notamment les contours doctrinaux de la musique et du chant en islam, avec l’apport des savants. Le troisième axe s’intéresse au défi de la relève, en mettant l’accent sur les difficultés rencontrées par les jeunes acteurs culturels musulmans qui souhaitent conjuguer expression artistique et exigences de la foi. Pour le coordonnateur du CCIB, la démarche ne se limite pas à un retour nostalgique vers les pratiques du passé. « Les raviver ne relève pas de la nostalgie, mais d’une approche stratégique de lutte contre l’extrémisme violent. C’est un pas audacieux et concret vers le renforcement de la cohésion sociale », a-t-il affirmé. « (…) Des armes de construction massive de la paix », Abdoulaye Dioni Au-delà de la préservation du patrimoine, les organisateurs veulent faire de ces journées un espace de transmission entre les générations. L’objectif est notamment de permettre aux jeunes de mieux connaître les pratiques culturelles d’inspiration islamique et les valeurs sociales qui leur étaient associées. Pour Abdoulaye Dioni, cette réappropriation culturelle peut contribuer à renforcer les repères des jeunes. « Ces chants et ces rythmes d’antan que nous cherchons à revitaliser ne sont pas obsolètes. Ils sont, au contraire, des armes de construction massive de la paix (…) nous devons documenter, préserver et redonner vie au Mansés, au Salou, au tarkaye, au dodo et à toutes ces sonorités qui chantent la paix, le respect de l’autre et l’amour de la patrie » , a-t-il déclaré. À travers ces deux journées, le CCIB ambitionne ainsi de contribuer à la valorisation du patrimoine culturel d’inspiration islamique et à la consolidation des liens entre les communautés. Les réflexions doivent également permettre de dégager des propositions concrètes pour favoriser la transmission de ces pratiques et leur réintégration dans certaines manifestations culturelles et religieuses. Faso7 L’article Sonorités traditionnelles d’inspiration islamique : Le CCIB mise sur le patrimoine pour renforcer le vivre-ensemble est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Mahama: Ghana’s cultural restitution drive rooted in dignity, not ownership
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has framed Ghana’s campaign for the return of cultural heritage as a question of dignity and historical justice rather than simply a dispute over legal ownership. Speaking in New York, President Mahama said the removal of African cultural objects during colonial conquest had separated communities from important elements of their history, identity and traditions. “This is not a story about static objects in museum cases. It is a story about people. It is a story about dignity. It is a story about an unfinished journey toward justice,” he said. He cited the 2024 return of a portion of Asante heritage, including the sacred Mpomponsuo sword, as an example of how restitution can reconnect living communities with traditions that remain relevant today. President Mahama said African cultural heritage should be understood as part of living societies rather than as relics belonging solely to the past. He called for stronger international cooperation to ensure that the return of such heritage becomes a structured process capable of restoring historical links between communities and their cultural institutions.

items.title: GoldBod resumes significant gold shipments, supporting reserves – BoG
items.description: Governor of the Bank of Ghana (BoG), Dr. Johnson Asiama, says the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) has resumed significant gold shipments, a development he says is supporting the country’s foreign exchange reserve accumulation. Speaking at the 132nd MPC press briefing, he explained that gold shipments had become less regular as of August compared with the previous two quarters, but assured that the situation has since improved. According to Dr Asiama, GoldBod exported a significant amount of gold in the past week, helping to strengthen the country’s reserve position. “The shipments have resumed. In fact, in the last week, Gold Board exported quite a significant amount of gold and this is supporting the reserves build-up,” he said. The Governor said the latest information on the shipments was received after the start of the Monetary Policy Committee’s meeting, changing the assessment of the situation compared with the data available at the beginning of the meeting. He noted that while the regularity of gold shipments had weakened as of August, the latest data shows that exports have picked up again. Dr Asiama said the development does not currently pose a significant risk to Ghana’s reserve accumulation, stressing that the key risk lies instead in movements in international gold prices. “What poses a risk is the international gold price out there, and you know that one is not within our control,” he said. He explained that global factors, including movements in US monetary policy, can influence gold prices and subsequently affect the value of Ghana’s gold exports and reserve accumulation. The Governor said that as long as international gold prices remain supportive, the Bank expects gold shipments to continue contributing to the build-up of Ghana’s reserves. The development comes as the Bank of Ghana continues to prioritise reserve accumulation as part of its foreign exchange management strategy. Dr Asiama has also indicated that GoldBod is expected to play a greater role in the intermediation segment of the Bank’s evolving foreign exchange management framework. The Bank is currently engaging GoldBod to finalise the new framework, with details expected to be communicated to the market once the arrangements are completed.

items.title: CNN, MS NOW, Politico request court hearing after White House access denied despite judge's order
items.description: CNN , MS NOW and Politico requested an urgent court hearing on Thursday after their reporters were barred from the White House despite a judge’s order that their access be restored. “This morning journalists from each of CNN , MS NOW , and Politico attempted to enter the White House and were turned away,” the news outlets said in a court filing. “Plaintiffs respectfully request that the court set a hearing by video conference or teleconference as soon as possible,” they said. “Defendants have already repeatedly violated the court’s order.” District Judge Timothy Kelly ruled overnight that the three news organisations banned by US President Donald Trump last week should have their access to the White House immediately restored. Revoking their press credentials “likely violated their constitutional due process rights,” Kelly said. “The ‘general rule’ is that ‘individuals must receive notice and an opportunity to be heard before the government deprives them’ of a constitutionally protected interest.” Trump has long attacked news outlets that have aired critical coverage of him, repeatedly blasting the press as the “ enemy of the people ”. CNN , MS NOW and Politico were barred from the White House on Friday for distributing what the Republican president branded “fake news” and “fiction and lies.” They filed a joint lawsuit asking for a temporary restraining order against the ban on the grounds that it violates the First Amendment of the US Constitution, which upholds the right to a free press. Ahead of the ruling, the Department of Justice had argued that Trump can “control reporters’ access to restricted presidential areas, such as the Oval Office.” “Access to the White House is a privilege — not a right,” it said. National security? The White House Press Office accused CNN in a letter to the cable news outlet of “trafficking in verifiable falsehoods about national security and other issues, and publishing sensitive or classified information,” with similar accusations leveled against MS NOW and Politico . The letter to CNN cited several stories about the US-Israeli war on Iran and a story on Trump’s plans to build a military bunker below the planned East Wing ballroom which allegedly “disclosed ‘top-secret’ construction details”. Kelly, who was appointed by Trump during his first term, appeared unconvinced. “The court is skeptical — at least on this record — that defendants’ interest in safeguarding national security is the actual motivation for, or is even advanced by, the revocation of plaintiffs’ hard passes,” the judge said. In a rare move, the top five US broadcasters said that they were halting pool coverage of the White House — where a broadcaster films on behalf of all television outlets for the day — in solidarity with CNN . “The public has a vital interest in receiving accurate, independent information about its government. No administration should restrict a news organisation because it objects to its reporting,” ABC , CBS , CNN , Fox and NBC said. In their request to Kelly to hold an emergency hearing on Thursday, the media outlets said “time is of the essence”. “ CNN is scheduled to be the television pool this evening for (Chinese) President Xi Jinping’s visit to the White House,” they said.

items.title: Ogou : Des tables-bancs au CEG Datcha Campement
items.description: Atakpamé, 24 sept. (ATOP) – Le maire de la commune Ogou 2, le professeur Dandonougbo Iléri en partenariat avec l’ONG Association de soutien aux enfants démunis (ASAED), a offert le jeudi, 24 septembre un lot de 20 tables-bancs au profit des apprenants du CEG Datcha Campement. Cette initiative vise à pallier le déficit d’équipements et à garantir aux élèves un cadre d’étude propice à la réussite scolaire. Ce don en tables-bancs fait suite à l’ouverture officielle dudit établissement à cette rentrée scolaire le 14 septembre 2026. Vue partielle des tables bancs Le maire de la commune Ogou 2, le professeur Dandonougbo Ileri, a salué l’ONG ASEAD pour ce partenariat fructueux axé sur l’avenir de la jeunesse. « Votre geste vient répondre à un besoin réel de notre école. Il s’agit d’un investissement concret en faveur de l’éducation et de l’avenir de notre jeunesse. À travers ce don, nous voyons une marque d’attention, de solidarité et d’engagement pour le développement éducatif », a-t-il indiqué. Le maire a exhorté les élèves au travail et surtout à l’excellence. Le chef d’inspection du secondaire Gnakouafre Eténi, a rassuré sur un usage pérenne des équipements. « Au nom de toute la communauté éducative, des enseignants et des élèves, nous vous assurons que ces tables-bancs seront utilisées avec soin et entretenues afin de servir durablement aux générations futures », a-t-il souligné. La cérémonie s’est déroulée en présence des autorités administratives, politiques et militaires. ATOP/KKT/HKM

items.title: Législatives 2026: Benkirane exclut une participation du PJD au gouvernement
items.description: Au lendemain des élections législatives qui ont placé le Parti Authenticité et Modernité (PAM) en tête du scrutin, le secrétaire général du Parti de la justice et du développement (PJD), Abdelilah Benkirane, a exclu toute participation de sa formation au futur gouvernement. Il a parallèlement appelé le Conseil national du parti à se réunir samedi prochain afin d’évaluer les résultats électoraux et de définir les orientations de la prochaine étape. S’exprimant au sujet des performances de son parti, Benkirane a estimé que le PJD sortait victorieux de cette échéance électorale, même s’il reconnaît avoir espéré un résultat plus important. Selon lui, la participation politique du parti demeure guidée par une même finalité : « servir la nation, la religion et la monarchie ». Le dirigeant islamiste est allé plus loin en affirmant que le « véritable grand vainqueur » du scrutin était le PJD. À ses yeux, le parti est parvenu, au cours des trois dernières années, à retrouver une place centrale dans le débat public, jusqu’à redevenir un acteur majeur de la vie politique nationale. Dans cette perspective, Abdelilah Benkirane considère que le PJD n’a pas vocation à intégrer l’exécutif qui devrait être formé sous la conduite du PAM. Une telle participation conduirait, selon lui, à une configuration gouvernementale « déséquilibrée ». Le secrétaire général du PJD a également exprimé de fortes réserves à l’égard de la future majorité. Il a qualifié le prochain gouvernement de « sujet à caution », estimant que la victoire du PAM aurait été « entachée » par des irrégularités électorales. Selon lui, des « acteurs partisans » seraient intervenus dans les urnes, une accusation qu’il a déjà formulée au cours de la soirée électorale. Dans le même registre, Benkirane s’est dit convaincu que le futur exécutif ne parviendra pas à atteindre ses objectifs, qualifiant le parti appelé à le diriger de « dangereux ». Évoquant ses rapports avec Fouzi Lekjaa, président du PAM, il a tenu à distinguer les relations personnelles des divergences politiques. S’il affirme entretenir avec lui des relations cordiales, il considère que son engagement au sein d’un parti qu’il juge porteur de « nombreux défauts » impose une opposition politique claire. Le chef du PJD a néanmoins vu dans les résultats de son parti un signe de redressement après la débâcle électorale de 2021. Selon lui, le score enregistré lors de ces législatives marque une rupture avec cet épisode et permet au parti de « tourner définitivement la page » de ce revers. The post Législatives 2026: Benkirane exclut une participation du PJD au gouvernement appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Trump hails 'truly great friendship' with Xi as Chinese president accorded lavish White House welcome
items.description: United States President Donald Trump hailed his “great friendship” with Xi Jinping on Thursday as he gave the Chinese leader a lavish welcome to the White House for a historic state visit. “President Xi and I have forged a friendship — a truly great friendship, actually — built on mutual respect and the vital interests of our people,” Trump said as he and Xi delivered remarks in the White House. Trump said he would discuss “pressing issues”, including artificial intelligence (AI), in talks with Xi. “During this visit, we will also discuss pressing issues concerning security, technology, and super intelligence — SI. The decisions we make in these areas today can promote peace and prosperity for decades and decades to come,” Trump said. In his remarks, Xi said that Washington and Beijing have a responsibility to “develop and manage AI for good”. “We have both the capability and responsibility to develop and manage AI for good and ensure that the development of AI is always under human control,” he said at the White House. Trump had personally greeted Xi on the tarmac earlier, the first time in more than six decades that a US president has welcomed a foreign political leader at Joint Base Andrews near Washington. He will lay on more pomp and ceremony on Thursday, treating his guest to talks in the Oval Office and finally a grand state banquet. The state dinner will feature a host of top US tech and AI company bosses — although Xi’s delegation includes no chief executive officers (CEOs), sources told AFP . Trump confirmed that his stalled Iran war would be discussed, despite earlier playing down reports that claimed that Beijing was giving Tehran intelligence. AI is a key focus due to growing fears that it is out of control and even risks wiping out humanity as China and the US race for supremacy in the field. Taiwan will also be on the cards, with Trump’s words likely to be watched for any sign of diminishing US support for the self-governing island that Beijing claims as its territory. The programme includes a military inspection in the Rose Garden — which Trump recently paved over — and a gift-giving ceremony involving Trump’s wife Melania and Xi’s wife Peng Liyuan. Xi’s visit will wrap up on Friday morning when the two presidential couples have tea at the White House and then visit the National Archives, home to the US Declaration of Independence. ‘A great greeting’ Trump and Melania had met the Chinese presidential couple on a red carpet at Joint Base Andrews, before a military band played the national anthems and US bombers roared overhead. “I thought it was a great little meeting, a great greeting, and I think they appreciate it,” Trump told reporters, brushing off the fact that Xi had not welcomed him at the airport for his Beijing state visit in May. Earlier, the US president sought to set the agenda by saying that both sides agreed no new controls were needed on fast-evolving AI technology. “Super Intelligence (SI) will be a big topic of discussion, but I want to leave it exactly where it is,” Trump said on social media , using his new moniker for artificial intelligence. “That is China’s position also.” In another post , Trump said 73-year-old Xi looked “strong, vibrant, and fit”, following recent rumours about the Chinese leader’s health. Xi urged cooperation in comments reported by Chinese state media shortly after his arrival, saying that China and the United States should be “partners rather than rivals”. Trade truce US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Wednesday announced a two-month extension of a trade truce that was due to expire in November. Both sides are keen to avoid plunging back into the trade war sparked by the US president’s sweeping global tariffs last year. But while Trump, 80, boasts that he will get results from what he calls his “great relationship” with Xi, few breakthroughs are expected. Instead, their third meeting since Trump returned to power is aimed at maintaining the broader detente. Xi’s first White House state visit in more than a decade will therefore be more about spectacle than substance.

items.title: FX interventions are rules-based, not discretionary-BoG
items.description: The Governor of the Bank of Ghana (BoG), Dr. Johnson Asiama, says the central bank’s interventions in the foreign exchange market are guided by a clear, rules-based framework and are not undertaken at the Governor’s discretion. He explained that the framework, introduced last year, provides defined conditions for when the Bank of Ghana should intervene in the foreign exchange market. Speaking at the 132nd MPC press briefing Dr Asiama said, the framework is designed to guide the Bank’s operations while allowing market forces to determine the exchange rate. “It’s not for me to just get up and say intervene. No. It’s a clear rules-based system that we use to determine when we need to intervene,” he said. The Governor noted that the framework has three key segments: reserve accumulation, intervention and intermediation. He said the Bank is currently working to transition the framework, with the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) expected to play a greater role in the intermediation segment. “We are in touch with Gold Board trying to perfect that new framework. And when we are ready, when it is done, we will communicate this to the market,” Dr Asiama said. He assured market participants that the Bank of Ghana will continue to perform its intervention role, but stressed that its primary objective remains building adequate foreign exchange reserves. “Our prime objective is to build adequate reserves at all times, because that is what supports our resilience as a country,” he added. The Governor’s comments come as the Bank continues to manage foreign exchange market conditions under its new FX operations framework. The framework, introduced in November 2025, emphasises a rules-based approach that allows exchange rates to be determined by market forces while seeking to limit excessive short-term volatility. Dr Asiama has previously disclosed that the Bank did not undertake direct FX market interventions between August 2024 and December 2025, with foreign exchange intermediation instead supported through the Domestic Gold Purchase Programme.

items.title: LHC turns down request for immediate suspension of Noreen and Uzma's detention, issues notices on plea
items.description: LAHORE: The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Thursday turned down a request to immediately suspend the preventive detention notifications issued against Noreen Niazi and Dr Uzma Khan, sisters of PTI founder Imran Khan. Uzma and Noreen were taken into custody on Monday for 30 days under the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance 1960 (MPO) just a day after their sister Aleema Khan was detained . The arrests of Imran’s sisters and other party leaders come ahead of the PTI’s Sept 27 countrywide protest and march to Islamabad. On Thursday, Justice Abher Gul Khan took up a petition challenging Uzma and Noreen’s detention, filed by the latter’s daughter Sakeena Niazi. Appearing as their counsel, Barrister Taimur Malik and Advocate Rana Mudassir argued that both women were “nonpolitical” and had been detained despite having no justification for their detention. They informed the court that Uzma had already been acquitted in a case registered against her, and a copy of the trial court’s decision declaring her innocent was on the case record. The lawyers also presented copies of two orders recently passed by the LHC’s Multan bench setting aside preventive detention of as many persons affiliated with PTI. The counsel requested the court to immediately suspend the detention notifications for Uzma and Noreen. Justice Abher, however, said the court would first seek a report from the relevant parties and hear their position before deciding the request for suspension. The court then issued notices to the respondents and sought their replies on the petition. The respondents included the Lahore deputy commissioner (DC) and capital city police officer (CCPO), the Home Department secretary, and the Kot Lakhpat jail superintendent. Hearing a petition against the detention of Aleema and her driver on Tuesday, Justice Abher had sought arguments on the plea’s maintainability. The court is set to resume the hearing on Friday. In the capital, the Islamabad High Court (IHC) had summoned the senior superintendent of police (operations) to appear on Thursday in a petition concerning alleged harassment of PTI leaders and raids on their homes. IG warns against violating law Separately, Punjab Inspector General (IG) Rao Abdul Kareem warned that anyone violating the law on Sept 27 would be dealt with strictly. The Punjab government has already imposed a ban on gatherings across the province for 13 days and prohibited inciting people to unlawful assembly. A similar ban under Section 144 has been enforced in Islamabad too. It has also requested deployment of Rangers in Rawalpindi, Attock, Jhelum and Mianwali districts until Oct 5, as well as sought downgrade of mobile and internet services at specific locations in Rawalpindi and Attock on Sept 27. Speaking to reporters after appearing before the LHC on Thursday, IG Kareem said he wanted to convey a clear message that no one would be allowed to take the law into their hands. Responding to a query, he said permission was required for holding a peaceful protest and pointed out that restrictions under Section 144 were currently imposed in the province. Asked whether any application had been submitted seeking permission for a protest, the police chief said he was not aware of any such request and that the DC concerned could better answer the question. The Punjab IG maintained that no one would be subjected to discriminatory treatment and that citizens would be dealt with without distinction as per the law. The PTI has called for a nationwide protest on Sept 27 to demand Imran’s release from jail and mobilise people for the supremacy of the Constitution. The government has warned against marching towards the federal capital or blocking roads there, with Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi cautioning PTI “not to enter a dead-end street” and hinting at a “permanent solution” to such protests. Hearing a plea against the march, the IHC on September 14 ruled that no political party or its leadership has the “lawful right to occupy public roads, highways, interchanges, toll plazas and buildings in Islamabad”. Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb on Sunday contended that strikes, sit-ins, long marches and road closures could cause an estimated Rs120 billion loss to the economy each day. Jamaat-i-Islami (JI), which had launched a march towards Islamabad against the petroleum levy, postponed the move at the request of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, pending a meeting with him.

items.title: DVLA explains delinquency charges related to expired driver’s licences
items.description: The Driver and Vehicle Licensing Authority (DVLA) has clarified the legal basis for delinquency charges imposed on motorists who fail to renew their driver’s licences before expiry. In a statement issued on September 24, the DVLA said the charges are provided for under the Road Traffic Regulations, 2026 (LI 2519) and the Fees and Charges (Miscellaneous Provisions) (Amendment) Regulations, 2025 (LI 2512). The Authority said motorists are responsible for ensuring that their licences remain valid and should renew them within one month before the expiry date. Under the regulations, licences must be renewed every two years and replaced after six years from the date of issue. Licence holders are also required to renew personally after passing an eye test and providing evidence of training with a certified driver training institution. The DVLA listed the delinquency charges for late renewals as follows: One sticker: GH¢52 Two stickers: GH¢104 Seven to 12 months overdue: GH¢75 More than one year to two years overdue: GH¢111 More than two years overdue: GH¢148 The Authority urged motorists to renew their licences on time to avoid the additional charges. It also disclosed that it sends SMS reminders to licence holders one month and two weeks before expiry, using the telephone numbers provided during the application process. The DVLA said the clarification was intended to address concerns over charges at its service centres and reiterated its commitment to maintaining high driving standards.

items.title: Législatives : Lachgar constate le recul de l’USFP et annonce une évaluation interne
items.description: Au lendemain des élections législatives, l’Union socialiste des forces populaires (USFP) a reconnu un net recul de ses performances électorales. Son premier secrétaire, Driss Lachgar, a estimé que les résultats provisoires du scrutin marquent une baisse par rapport aux précédentes échéances, tout en assurant que le parti procédera à une analyse approfondie de la situation au sein de ses instances. S’exprimant devant la presse dans la nuit de mercredi à jeudi, après l’annonce des résultats provisoires, le dirigeant socialiste a déclaré qu’« il ne fait aucun doute que les résultats du parti lors de ces élections législatives constituent un recul par rapport à ceux que nous avions obtenus auparavant ». Face à ce constat, la direction de l’USFP prévoit de se réunir dans les prochains jours afin d’examiner les résultats et d’en tirer les enseignements. Cette évaluation se fera, selon Driss Lachgar, « à la lumière des développements que connaîtront les prochains jours ». D’après les résultats provisoires publiés à l’issue du scrutin, l’USFP a obtenu 26 sièges à la Chambre des représentants. Le Parti Authenticité et Modernité (PAM) est arrivé en tête avec 97 sièges.
